source.text: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι εἰσίν τινες τῶν ὧδε ἑστηκότων οἵτινες οὐ μὴ γεύσωνται θανάτου ἕως ἂν ἴδωσιν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐληλυθυῖαν ἐν δυνάμει.

records.literal_gloss: And he was saying to them, Truly I say to you that there are some of those here standing who no not shall taste of death until they see the kingdom of God having come with power.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying to them, "Truly I say to you that there are some of those standing here who will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God having come with power."
en.B: He went on to say to them, "Truly I tell you, some who stand here will not taste death until the kingdom of God has come in power and they have seen it."
en.R: Then Jesus told them, "I tell you the truth: some people standing here will not die until they see the kingdom of God come with power."

es.L: Y les decía: «En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que hay algunos de los que están aquí de pie que de ningún modo probarán la muerte hasta que vean el reino de Dios venido con poder».
es.B: Y les siguió diciendo: «En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que algunos de los que están aquí no probarán la muerte hasta que el reino de Dios haya venido con poder y ellos lo hayan visto».
es.R: Luego Jesús les dijo: «{{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: algunas de las personas que están aquí no morirán antes de ver el reino de Dios venir con poder».

sw.L: Naye alikuwa akiwaambia, "Kweli nawaambia kwamba kuna baadhi ya wale waliosimama hapa ambao hawataonja kifo kamwe mpaka wauone ufalme wa Mungu ukiwa umekuja kwa nguvu."
sw.B: Akaendelea kuwaambia, "Kweli nawaambia, baadhi ya wale waliosimama hapa hawataonja kifo mpaka wauone ufalme wa Mungu umekwisha kuja kwa nguvu."
sw.R: Kisha Yesu akawaambia, "Nawaambia ukweli, baadhi ya watu waliosimama hapa hawatakufa kabla ya kuuona ufalme wa Mungu ukija kwa nguvu."

decisions.choice: the kingdom come with power: most likely what the three disciples see on the mountain six days later (9:2-8), a first view of the kingdom in power
alternatives: Jesus' resurrection and the coming of the Spirit
the final coming of the Son of Man in 8:38
decisions.reason: Mark sets this saying directly before the transfiguration and ties the two together with "after six days" (9:2). Only "some" will see it, and only three disciples go up the mountain. Others read the saying as pointing to the resurrection and what followed it, or to the final coming spoken of in 8:38. The text does not settle the question.

decisions.choice: taste death: die
decisions.reason: To taste death is a way of saying to experience death, to die.

decisions.choice: will not: a double negative, a strong denial
decisions.reason: Two negatives together make a firm promise: they will certainly not die first.

decisions.choice: having come: a perfect participle, the kingdom seen as already arrived
decisions.reason: They will see the kingdom as something that has come and is present in power.

decisions.choice: he was saying to them: the saying closes the teaching of 8:34-38
alternatives: the start of a new scene
decisions.reason: The chapter break comes in the middle of a speech. Jesus is still speaking to the crowd and the disciples of 8:34.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: The same forms as at 3:28. Readable says "not die" for the idiom "taste death".

decisions.choice: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo (L, B); {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad (R)
decisions.reason: The rendering of Jesus's single amen used through the Gospels, recorded once in this chapter. "De cierto" is the older form and now sounds dated.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on separate pronouns and possessives
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun out ("les decía") and joins some object pronouns to the verb ("escúchenlo", "preguntarle"), where there is nothing separate to capitalise. So the setting covers fewer words than in English, as in Mark 16. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: Kweli nawaambia (L, B); Nawaambia ukweli (R)
decisions.reason: The rendering of Jesus's single amen used through the Gospels, recorded once in this chapter; John's double form is "Kweli kweli nawaambia".

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on free pronouns and possessives
decisions.reason: The English Literal "he was saying" takes the setting. Swahili carries Jesus in the verb prefix ("alikuwa akiwaambia"), which cannot take a capital, so the setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives, as in John. Swahili has fewer spans than English through the chapter.

source.text: Καὶ μετὰ ἡμέρας ἓξ παραλαμβάνει ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὸν Πέτρον καὶ τὸν Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην, καὶ ἀναφέρει αὐτοὺς εἰς ὄρος ὑψηλὸν κατ’ ἰδίαν μόνους.

records.literal_gloss: And after days six takes along Jesus Peter and James and John, and brings up them into a mountain high, apart, alone.

en.L: And after six days Jesus takes along Peter and James and John and brings them up onto a high mountain, apart, by themselves.
en.B: Six days later Jesus took Peter, James and John with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and led them up a high mountain, away from everyone else.
en.R: Six days later, Jesus took Peter, James, and John with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and they climbed a high mountain. Only the four of them were there.

es.L: Y después de seis días, Jesús toma consigo a Pedro, a Santiago y a Juan, y los lleva arriba a un monte alto, aparte, solos.
es.B: Seis días después, Jesús llevó consigo a Pedro, a Santiago y a Juan, y los hizo subir a un monte alto, lejos de todos los demás.
es.R: Seis días más tarde, Jesús se llevó consigo a Pedro, a Santiago y a Juan, y subieron a un monte alto. Solo estaban allí ellos cuatro.

sw.L: Na baada ya siku sita Yesu anawachukua Petro na Yakobo na Yohana, na anawapandisha juu ya mlima mrefu, faraghani, wao peke yao.
sw.B: Siku sita baadaye, Yesu aliwachukua Petro, Yakobo na Yohana, akawapeleka juu ya mlima mrefu, mbali na watu wengine wote.
sw.R: Siku sita baadaye, Yesu aliwachukua Petro, Yakobo na Yohana, wakapanda mlima mrefu. Walikuwa wao wanne tu pale.

decisions.choice: takes along, brings up: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: As often in Mark, past events are told in the present tense to make them vivid. The sense is past: he took them and led them up.

decisions.choice: after six days: counted from the sayings of 8:27-9:1; it may also recall Moses on Mount Sinai
decisions.reason: Mark rarely gives exact times. In Exodus 24:15-16 the cloud covered Sinai for six days before God called Moses out of the cloud. With the cloud and the voice in 9:7, the echo may be intended.

decisions.choice: a high mountain: Mark does not name it
decisions.reason: Later tradition named Mount Tabor in Galilee. Mount Hermon lies near Caesarea Philippi, where the last scene took place (8:27). Mark leaves it unnamed.

decisions.choice: apart, alone: privately, just the four of them
decisions.reason: Two phrases together stress that no one else was there, as in 4:34 and 6:31.

decisions.choice: Only the four of them were there
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly who was on the mountain.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (toma, lleva); pretérito at Balanced and Readable (llevó, hizo subir)
decisions.reason: Mark tells much of the story in the present (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past, as Spanish narrative does. The same through the chapter.

decisions.choice: consigo, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The English "with him" takes the setting. Spanish says it with the reflexive "consigo", one word that cannot be capitalised in part, as in Matthew 17:1.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (anawachukua, anawapandisha); past at Balanced and Readable (aliwachukua, akawapeleka)
decisions.reason: Mark tells much of the story in the present (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the narrative past, with -li- for the first verb and -ka- for those that follow. The same through the chapter.

source.text: καὶ μετεμορφώθη ἔμπροσθεν αὐτῶν, καὶ τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο στίλβοντα λευκὰ λίαν οἷα γναφεὺς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς οὐ δύναται οὕτως λευκᾶναι.

records.literal_gloss: And he was transfigured before them, \v 3 and the garments of him became shining, white exceedingly, such as a launderer on the earth not is able thus to whiten.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was transfigured before them, \v 3 and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} garments became shining, exceedingly white, such as no launderer on earth is able to whiten [them].
en.B: There {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was transfigured in front of them. \v 3 His clothes turned dazzling and intensely white, white beyond what any launderer on earth could achieve.
en.R: There, while they watched, Jesus' appearance was changed. \v 3 His clothes began to shine. They became whiter than anyone on earth could ever wash them.

es.L: Y fue transfigurado delante de ellos, \v 3 y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} vestidos se volvieron resplandecientes, sumamente blancos, tanto como ningún lavandero en la tierra puede blanquear[los].
es.B: Allí fue transfigurado delante de ellos. \v 3 Su ropa se volvió resplandeciente y blanquísima, más blanca de lo que ningún lavandero en la tierra podría dejarla.
es.R: Allí, mientras ellos miraban, Jesús fue transformado. \v 3 Su ropa empezó a brillar. Se volvió más blanca de lo que nadie en la tierra podría lavarla.

sw.L: Na akabadilishwa sura mbele yao, \v 3 na mavazi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} yakawa yanang'aa, meupe mno, kiasi ambacho hakuna dobi duniani awezaye kuyafanya meupe hivyo.
sw.B: Huko alibadilishwa sura mbele yao. \v 3 Mavazi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} yakawa ya kung'aa na meupe kabisa, meupe kuliko dobi yeyote duniani anavyoweza kuyang'arisha.
sw.R: Huko, walipokuwa wakitazama, Yesu alibadilishwa sura. \v 3 Nguo {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} zilianza kung'aa. Zikawa nyeupe kuliko mtu yeyote duniani anavyoweza kuzifua.

decisions.choice: transfigured: his form was changed so that a heavenly glory showed
alternatives: he only looked different in the light
decisions.reason: The verb means to change form. Paul uses it of believers being changed into the Lord's likeness (2 Corinthians 3:18). Mark describes only the clothes, but the change is in Jesus himself.

decisions.choice: was transfigured: a passive, God is the one who changed him
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the actor unnamed, a common way of speaking of God's action.

decisions.choice: launderer: a fuller, who cleaned and bleached new wool and cloth
decisions.reason: Fullers whitened cloth with lye and fuller's earth. Even their best work could not match this whiteness.

decisions.choice: shining white clothes: the clothing of heaven
decisions.reason: White clothing marks God and heavenly beings (Daniel 7:9; Mark 16:5).

decisions.choice: transfigured
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the word long used for this event. Readable says what it means: his appearance was changed.

decisions.choice: fue transfigurado (L, B); fue transformado (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is passive: God is the one who changed him (meaning decision m2). The Spanish passive keeps that, where the reflexive "se transfiguró" would make Jesus the one who acted. Readable uses the everyday "transformado", as in Matthew 17:2.

decisions.choice: akabadilishwa sura (L); alibadilishwa sura (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is passive: God is the one who changed him (meaning decision m2). The passive "alibadilishwa" keeps that, where "akageuka sura" (his appearance changed) would make Jesus the one who acted, as in Matthew 17:2.

source.text: καὶ ὤφθη αὐτοῖς Ἠλίας σὺν Μωϋσεῖ, καὶ ἦσαν συλλαλοῦντες τῷ Ἰησοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And appeared to them Elijah with Moses, and they were talking with Jesus.

en.L: And Elijah with Moses appeared to them, and they were talking with Jesus.
en.B: Then Elijah appeared to them along with Moses, and the two were talking with Jesus.
en.R: Then the disciples saw Elijah and Moses there. These two great men from long ago were talking with Jesus.

es.L: Y se les apareció Elías con Moisés, y estaban conversando con Jesús.
es.B: Entonces se les apareció Elías junto con Moisés, y los dos conversaban con Jesús.
es.R: Entonces los discípulos vieron allí a Elías y a Moisés. Estos dos grandes hombres de hace mucho tiempo estaban hablando con Jesús.

sw.L: Na Eliya pamoja na Musa wakawatokea, nao walikuwa wakizungumza na Yesu.
sw.B: Kisha Eliya aliwatokea pamoja na Musa, nao wawili walikuwa wakizungumza na Yesu.
sw.R: Kisha wanafunzi waliwaona Eliya na Musa pale. Watu hawa wawili wakuu wa zamani walikuwa wakiongea na Yesu.

decisions.choice: Elijah and Moses: the great prophet and the giver of the law
decisions.reason: Malachi 4:4-5 names Moses and Elijah together at the close of the prophets. Both met God on a mountain (Exodus 24; 1 Kings 19:8), and neither had an ordinary burial (Deuteronomy 34:6; 2 Kings 2:11).

decisions.choice: Elijah with Moses: Elijah is named first
decisions.reason: Mark names Elijah first. Elijah's coming is what the disciples ask about on the way down (9:11-13).

decisions.choice: appeared: they were seen, a word used of heavenly appearances
decisions.reason: The word means was seen. It is used of appearances from God, such as the risen Jesus (1 Corinthians 15:5).

decisions.choice: the disciples saw; these two great men from long ago
decisions.reason: Readable names who saw them and says who Elijah and Moses were.

source.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Πέτρος λέγει τῷ Ἰησοῦ· Ῥαββί, καλόν ἐστιν ἡμᾶς ὧδε εἶναι, καὶ ποιήσωμεν τρεῖς σκηνάς, σοὶ μίαν καὶ Μωϋσεῖ μίαν καὶ Ἠλίᾳ μίαν.

records.literal_gloss: And answering Peter says to Jesus, Rabbi, good it is for us here to be, and let us make three tents, for you one and for Moses one and for Elijah one.

en.L: And Peter responds and says to Jesus, "Rabbi, it is good for us to be here, and let us make three tents, one for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and one for Moses and one for Elijah."
en.B: Peter spoke up and said to Jesus, "Rabbi, how good it is that we are here! Let us set up three shelters, one for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and one for Moses and one for Elijah."
en.R: Peter said to Jesus, "Teacher, this is a good place for us to be. We will make three shelters. One will be for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, another for Moses, and a third for Elijah."

es.L: Y respondiendo Pedro, dice a Jesús: «Rabí, es bueno que nosotros estemos aquí; hagamos tres tiendas, una para {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, una para Moisés y una para Elías».
es.B: Pedro tomó la palabra y dijo a Jesús: «Rabí, ¡qué bueno que estemos aquí! Levantemos tres chozas: una para {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, otra para Moisés y otra para Elías».
es.R: Pedro le dijo a Jesús: «Maestro, este es un buen lugar para nosotros. Haremos tres chozas. Una será para {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, otra para Moisés y otra para Elías».

sw.L: Na Petro akijibu anamwambia Yesu, "Rabi, ni vyema sisi kuwa hapa; na tufanye hema tatu, moja kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}, na moja kwa ajili ya Musa, na moja kwa ajili ya Eliya."
sw.B: Petro alimwambia Yesu, "Rabi, ni vizuri kama nini kwamba tuko hapa! Tujenge vibanda vitatu: kimoja kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}, kimoja kwa ajili ya Musa, na kimoja kwa ajili ya Eliya."
sw.R: Petro alimwambia Yesu, "Mwalimu, hapa ni mahali pazuri kwetu kuwa. Tutajenga vibanda vitatu. Kimoja kitakuwa {{deity_pronoun:chako|Chako}}, kingine cha Musa, na kingine cha Eliya."

decisions.choice: answering: speaking up, though no question was asked
decisions.reason: The word often simply introduces what someone says in response to a situation.

decisions.choice: Rabbi: a Hebrew title of respect, my master, used for a teacher
decisions.reason: The title means my great one. It was used for teachers of the law and is the first time Mark uses it for Jesus.

decisions.choice: tents: shelters, such as huts of branches
decisions.reason: The word means a tent or booth. Peter seems to want to keep the moment and the visitors there.

decisions.choice: tents: perhaps recalling the Festival of Booths or the tent where God met Moses
decisions.reason: Israel lived in shelters at the Festival of Booths (Leviticus 23:42-43), and God spoke with Moses in a tent (Exodus 33:7-11). Mark does not say what Peter had in mind.

decisions.choice: one for you, one for Moses, one for Elijah: Peter puts the three side by side
decisions.reason: Peter treats the three as equals. The voice from the cloud corrects this (9:7).

decisions.choice: shelters
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a word for a simple temporary structure. Readable also says "Teacher" for the Hebrew title Rabbi.

decisions.choice: tiendas (L); chozas (B, R)
decisions.reason: Peter means simple shelters such as huts of branches (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps "tiendas", the word for the Greek; Balanced and Readable say "chozas", as the English says "shelters" and as in Matthew 17:4.

decisions.choice: hema (L); vibanda (B, R)
decisions.reason: Peter means simple shelters such as huts of branches (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps "hema", the word for the Greek "tents"; Balanced and Readable say "vibanda" (huts), as the English says "shelters" and as in Matthew 17:4.

source.text: οὐ γὰρ ᾔδει τί ἀποκριθῇ, ἔκφοβοι γὰρ ἐγένοντο.

records.literal_gloss: Not for he knew what he should answer, terrified for they became.

en.L: For he did not know what he should answer, for they had become terrified.
en.B: He did not know what to say, because they were all badly frightened.
en.R: Peter did not know what to say, because the three of them were very afraid.

es.L: Pues no sabía qué responder, porque se habían llenado de terror.
es.B: No sabía qué decir, porque todos estaban muy asustados.
es.R: Pedro no sabía qué decir, porque los tres tenían mucho miedo.

sw.L: Kwa maana hakujua la kujibu, kwa kuwa walikuwa wameingiwa na hofu kuu.
sw.B: Hakujua aseme nini, kwa sababu wote walikuwa wameogopa sana.
sw.R: Petro hakujua aseme nini, kwa sababu wote watatu waliogopa sana.

decisions.choice: for ... for: Mark explains Peter's words
decisions.reason: Mark gives two reasons: Peter did not know what to say, and they were terrified. His offer came from fear and confusion.

decisions.choice: terrified: overcome with fear
decisions.reason: The word is a strong one, used of Moses trembling at Sinai (Hebrews 12:21).

decisions.choice: answer: respond, say
decisions.reason: As in 9:5, the verb means to speak in response to what was happening.

decisions.choice: Peter; the three of them
decisions.reason: Readable names who is meant.

source.text: καὶ ἐγένετο νεφέλη ἐπισκιάζουσα αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἐγένετο φωνὴ ἐκ τῆς νεφέλης· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, ἀκούετε αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And there came a cloud overshadowing them, and there came a voice out of the cloud, This is the Son of me, the beloved; listen to him.

en.L: And a cloud came, overshadowing them, and a voice came out of the cloud: "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Son, the beloved; listen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.B: Then a cloud came and cast its shadow over them, and a voice spoke from the cloud: "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} dearly loved Son. Listen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.R: Then a cloud came and covered them with its shadow. A voice came from the cloud and said, "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Son, and I love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Listen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"

es.L: Y vino una nube que los cubría con su sombra, y vino una voz desde la nube: «Este es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Hijo, el amado; {{plural_you:escúchenlo|escuchadlo}}».
es.B: Entonces vino una nube que los cubrió con su sombra, y desde la nube una voz dijo: «Este es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Hijo amado. {{plural_you:Escúchenlo|Escuchadlo}}».
es.R: Entonces vino una nube y los cubrió con su sombra. De la nube salió una voz que dijo: «Este es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Hijo, y yo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} amo. ¡{{plural_you:Escúchenlo|Escuchadlo}}!».

sw.L: Na likaja wingu likiwatia kivuli, na sauti ikaja kutoka katika wingu, "Huyu ni Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, mpendwa; msikilizeni {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}."
sw.B: Kisha wingu lilikuja, likawafunika kwa kivuli chake, na sauti ikasema kutoka katika wingu, "Huyu ni Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} mpendwa sana. Msikilizeni {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}."
sw.R: Kisha wingu likaja, likawafunika kwa kivuli chake. Sauti ilitoka katika wingu, ikasema, "Huyu ni Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} ninampenda. Msikilizeni {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}!"

decisions.choice: the cloud: the cloud of God's presence
decisions.reason: God came down in a cloud on Sinai and filled the tent of meeting with a cloud (Exodus 24:15-18; 40:34-35). The voice comes from the cloud, so the speaker is God.

decisions.choice: This is my Son, the beloved; listen to him: the words of 1:11 again, and the prophet like Moses
decisions.reason: The voice repeats what was said at Jesus' baptism (1:11; Psalm 2:7). "Listen to him" recalls Deuteronomy 18:15, where Moses says God will raise up a prophet like him, and Israel must listen to him.

decisions.choice: This is: the voice now speaks to the disciples about Jesus
decisions.reason: At the baptism the voice said "You are" to Jesus. Here it tells the three who he is and what they must do.

decisions.choice: overshadowing them: covering with its shadow, perhaps all on the mountain
decisions.reason: "Them" may mean Jesus with Moses and Elijah, or the disciples too. Mark does not make it clear.

decisions.choice: my dearly loved Son (B); my Son, and I love him (R)
decisions.reason: The same renderings as at 1:11.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:escúchenlo|escuchadlo}}
decisions.reason: The command is plural, spoken to the disciples (meaning decision m3), so it takes the ustedes / vosotros setting, as every plural "you" in this chapter does. English has no such choice. The pronoun is joined to the verb, so it carries no deity_pronoun span.

source.text: καὶ ἐξάπινα περιβλεψάμενοι οὐκέτι οὐδένα εἶδον ἀλλὰ τὸν Ἰησοῦν μόνον μεθ’ ἑαυτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And suddenly having looked around, no longer no one they saw except Jesus alone with themselves.

en.L: And suddenly, looking around, they no longer saw anyone with them except Jesus alone.
en.B: All at once they looked around and saw no one there with them any more, only Jesus.
en.R: Suddenly the disciples looked around. Moses and Elijah were gone. Only Jesus was there with them.

es.L: Y de repente, mirando alrededor, ya no vieron a nadie, sino solo a Jesús con ellos.
es.B: De pronto miraron a su alrededor y ya no vieron a nadie con ellos, sino solo a Jesús.
es.R: De repente, los discípulos miraron a su alrededor. Moisés y Elías ya no estaban. Solo Jesús estaba allí con ellos.

sw.L: Na ghafla, walipotazama pande zote, hawakumwona tena mtu yeyote, ila Yesu peke yake pamoja nao.
sw.B: Ghafla walipotazama huku na huku, hawakumwona tena mtu yeyote pamoja nao, ila Yesu tu.
sw.R: Ghafla wanafunzi walitazama huku na huku. Musa na Eliya walikuwa wametoweka. Yesu peke yake ndiye aliyekuwa pale pamoja nao.

decisions.choice: no longer ... no one: a double negative for emphasis
decisions.reason: The negatives strengthen each other: there was no one at all except Jesus.

decisions.choice: Jesus alone: the one they were told to listen to remains
decisions.reason: After the voice says "listen to him", Moses and Elijah are gone, and Jesus is left with them.

decisions.choice: Moses and Elijah were gone
decisions.reason: Readable says who had disappeared.

source.text: Καὶ καταβαινόντων αὐτῶν ἐκ τοῦ ὄρους διεστείλατο αὐτοῖς ἵνα μηδενὶ ἃ εἶδον διηγήσωνται, εἰ μὴ ὅταν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῇ.

records.literal_gloss: And descending of them from the mountain he instructed them that to no one what they had seen they should tell, except when the Son of Man out from [the] dead had risen.

en.L: And as they were coming down from the mountain, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} instructed them to tell no one what they had seen, except when the Son of Man had risen from [the] dead.
en.B: As they came down the mountain, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them orders not to describe what they had seen to anyone until the Son of Man rose from the dead.
en.R: On the way down the mountain, Jesus ordered them to keep what they had seen to themselves. They were to tell no one until the Son of Man had come back to life from death.

es.L: Y mientras bajaban del monte, les ordenó que a nadie contaran lo que habían visto, sino cuando el Hijo del Hombre hubiera resucitado de [entre los] muertos.
es.B: Mientras bajaban del monte, les ordenó que no contaran a nadie lo que habían visto, hasta que el Hijo del Hombre resucitara de entre los muertos.
es.R: Mientras bajaban del monte, Jesús les ordenó que no dijeran nada de lo que habían visto. No debían contárselo a nadie hasta que el Hijo del Hombre volviera a la vida de entre los muertos.

sw.L: Na walipokuwa wakishuka kutoka mlimani, aliwaagiza wasimweleze mtu yeyote yale waliyoyaona, isipokuwa wakati Mwana wa Adamu atakapokuwa amefufuka kutoka kwa wafu.
sw.B: Walipokuwa wakishuka mlimani, aliwaagiza wasimsimulie mtu yeyote yale waliyoyaona, mpaka Mwana wa Adamu atakapofufuka kutoka kwa wafu.
sw.R: Walipokuwa wakishuka kutoka mlimani, Yesu aliwaamuru wasiseme lolote kuhusu yale waliyoyaona. Wasimwambie mtu yeyote mpaka Mwana wa Adamu atakapofufuka kutoka kwa wafu.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus speaking of himself
decisions.reason: Jesus uses this title for himself, as in 8:31 and 8:38. It recalls the one like a son of man in Daniel 7:13-14.

decisions.choice: except when: the silence lasts only until the resurrection
decisions.reason: This is the only command to silence in Mark with a time limit. After the resurrection the event could be understood and told.

decisions.choice: risen from the dead: raised to life again
decisions.reason: The phrase means coming back to bodily life, as Jesus said in 8:31.

decisions.choice: They were to keep quiet until
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the sentence in two and states the time limit plainly.

decisions.choice: el Hijo del Hombre, with capitals and no gender setting
decisions.reason: The title used through the Gospels: Jesus speaks of himself (meaning decision m1), so it is never under the gender setting.

decisions.choice: Mwana wa Adamu
decisions.reason: The settled Swahili title, used through the Gospels as in John; "Adamu" is also a word for humankind. "Mwana wa Mtu" is more literal but unfamiliar. Jesus speaks of himself (meaning decision m1), so it is never under the gender setting.

source.text: καὶ τὸν λόγον ἐκράτησαν πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς συζητοῦντες τί ἐστιν τὸ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῆναι.

records.literal_gloss: And that saying they kept to themselves, questioning what is the out from [the] dead to rise.

en.L: And they kept the word to themselves, questioning what the rising from [the] dead is.
en.B: They kept the matter to themselves, but they debated with one another what this "rising from the dead" might mean.
en.R: So they did not tell anyone. But they talked with each other about what Jesus meant by "rising from the dead."

es.L: Y guardaron la palabra para sí, discutiendo qué es eso de resucitar de [entre los] muertos.
es.B: Ellos guardaron el asunto para sí, pero discutían entre ellos qué podría significar eso de «resucitar de entre los muertos».
es.R: Así que no se lo dijeron a nadie. Pero hablaban entre ellos sobre lo que Jesús quería decir con «resucitar de entre los muertos».

sw.L: Nao wakalishika neno hilo kati yao wenyewe, wakijadiliana maana ya kufufuka kutoka kwa wafu ni nini.
sw.B: Walilishika jambo hilo kuwa siri kati yao, lakini walijadiliana wao kwa wao kuhusu maana ya "kufufuka kutoka kwa wafu."
sw.R: Kwa hiyo hawakumwambia mtu yeyote. Lakini waliongea wao kwa wao kuhusu Yesu alimaanisha nini aliposema "kufufuka kutoka kwa wafu."

decisions.choice: to themselves: goes with kept, they told no one
alternatives: goes with questioning: they discussed it among themselves
decisions.reason: The phrase can belong with either verb. With "kept" it says they obeyed the order of 9:9; with "questioning" it says they discussed it among themselves. Both are true in the scene.

decisions.choice: the word: the saying, the command and what it said about rising
decisions.reason: The noun often means a matter or saying as a whole, as in 8:32.

decisions.choice: what rising from the dead is: they could not see how the Son of Man could rise before the end
alternatives: they did not believe in resurrection
decisions.reason: Many Jews expected all the righteous to rise together at the end of the age (Daniel 12:2). The disciples did not understand a single person rising first.

decisions.choice: what Jesus meant by
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that they were puzzling over Jesus' words.

source.text: καὶ ἐπηρώτων αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Ὅτι λέγουσιν οἱ γραμματεῖς ὅτι Ἠλίαν δεῖ ἐλθεῖν πρῶτον;

records.literal_gloss: And they were asking him, saying, Why say the scribes that Elijah it behooves to come first?

en.L: And they were asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?"
en.B: They asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Why do the scribes claim that Elijah has to come first?"
en.R: Then they asked Jesus, "Why do the teachers of God's law say that Elijah must come first?"

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaban, diciendo: «¿Por qué dicen los escribas que Elías tiene que venir primero?».
es.B: Entonces {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaron: «¿Por qué afirman los escribas que primero tiene que venir Elías?».
es.R: Entonces preguntaron a Jesús: «¿Por qué dicen los maestros de la ley que Elías tiene que venir primero?».

sw.L: Nao walikuwa wakimwuliza, wakisema, "Kwa nini waandishi husema kwamba ni lazima Eliya aje kwanza?"
sw.B: Walimwuliza, "Mbona waandishi hudai kwamba Eliya lazima aje kwanza?"
sw.R: Kisha wakamwuliza Yesu, "Kwa nini walimu wa sheria husema kwamba Eliya lazima aje kwanza?"

decisions.choice: why: the small word here opens a question
alternatives: that: introducing a statement, the scribes say that
decisions.reason: The word usually means "that", but at the head of a question it can mean "why", as in 9:28.

decisions.choice: Elijah must come first: the promise of Malachi 4:5-6
alternatives: a saying of the scribes only
decisions.reason: God promised to send Elijah the prophet before the great day of the Lord. The scribes taught that he would come first, before the Messiah.

decisions.choice: first: before the end, and before the Messiah
alternatives: before the Son of Man rises
decisions.reason: The disciples have just seen Elijah and heard Jesus speak of his own death and rising. They ask how this fits the order the scribes taught.

decisions.choice: the teachers of God's law
decisions.reason: As in earlier chapters, Readable says who the scribes were.

decisions.choice: los escribas (L, B); los maestros de la ley (R)
alternatives: los maestros de la ley (every level)
decisions.reason: The New Testament choice for Spanish: "escribas" is the familiar name for these experts in the Law of Moses; Readable says what they did, as the English Readable says "teachers of God's law". The same in verse 14.

decisions.choice: waandishi (L, B); walimu wa sheria (R)
decisions.reason: The New Testament choice for Swahili: "waandishi" is the familiar name for these experts in the Law of Moses; Readable says what they did, as the English Readable says "teachers of God's law". The same in verse 14.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἔφη αὐτοῖς· Ἠλίας μὲν ἐλθὼν πρῶτον ἀποκαθιστάνει πάντα, καὶ πῶς γέγραπται ἐπὶ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἵνα πολλὰ πάθῃ καὶ ἐξουδενηθῇ;

records.literal_gloss: And he was saying to them, Elijah indeed having come first restores all things; and how has it been written of the Son of Man that many things he should suffer and be set at naught?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Elijah indeed comes first and restores all things; and how is it written of the Son of Man that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} should suffer many things and be treated with contempt?
en.B: He told them, "Elijah does come first and set everything right. Then why does Scripture say that the Son of Man is to suffer much and be scorned?
en.R: Jesus answered, "It is true that Elijah comes first and makes everything right again. But then why do the Scriptures say that the Son of Man will suffer a great deal, and that people will treat {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as worthless?

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les dijo: «Elías, ciertamente, viniendo primero, restaura todas las cosas; ¿y cómo está escrito del Hijo del Hombre que padezca mucho y sea despreciado?
es.B: Él les dijo: «Es cierto que Elías viene primero y lo pone todo en orden. Entonces, ¿por qué dice la Escritura que el Hijo del Hombre tiene que sufrir mucho y ser despreciado?
es.R: Jesús respondió: «Es verdad que Elías viene primero y hace que todo vuelva a estar bien. Pero entonces, ¿por qué dicen las Escrituras que el Hijo del Hombre sufrirá mucho y que la gente {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} tratará como si no valiera nada?

sw.L: Naye akawaambia, "Kweli Eliya akija kwanza hurejesha mambo yote; na imeandikwaje kuhusu Mwana wa Adamu kwamba atateseka mambo mengi na kudharauliwa?
sw.B: Aliwaambia, "Ni kweli, Eliya huja kwanza na kuyaweka mambo yote sawa. Basi kwa nini Maandiko yanasema kwamba Mwana wa Adamu atateseka sana na kudharauliwa?
sw.R: Yesu akajibu, "Ni kweli kwamba Eliya huja kwanza na kufanya kila kitu kiwe sawa tena. Lakini basi, kwa nini Maandiko yanasema kwamba Mwana wa Adamu atateseka sana, na kwamba watu watamwona kuwa si kitu?

decisions.choice: indeed: Jesus grants the scribes' point
decisions.reason: The small word agrees with the statement before the next clause adds a "but".

decisions.choice: restores all things: puts all things back in right order
alternatives: brings the world to an end
decisions.reason: Malachi 4:6 says Elijah will turn the hearts of fathers to children and children to fathers.

decisions.choice: it is written: Scripture speaks of the suffering of the Son of Man
decisions.reason: Jesus does not name the passage. Isaiah 53:3 and Psalm 22 speak of one who is despised and suffers. Mark gives no single text.

decisions.choice: how: a question that sets two teachings side by side
decisions.reason: If Elijah sets everything right, why must the Son of Man suffer? Jesus' answer in 9:13 is that Elijah has come and was himself mistreated.

decisions.choice: be treated with contempt: be counted as nothing
decisions.reason: The verb means to treat as worthless. It is a different word from the one used for being rejected in 8:31.

decisions.choice: the Scriptures
decisions.reason: Readable names what is written.

source.text: ἀλλὰ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι καὶ Ἠλίας ἐλήλυθεν, καὶ ἐποίησαν αὐτῷ ὅσα ἤθελον, καθὼς γέγραπται ἐπ’ αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: But I say to you that also Elijah has come, and they did to him whatever they desired, as it has been written of him.

en.L: But I say to you that Elijah also has come, and they did to him whatever they wanted, just as it is written of him."
en.B: But I tell you that Elijah has in fact come, and they did to him as they pleased, just as it is written about him."
en.R: But I tell you, Elijah has already come. And people did whatever they wanted to him, just as the Scriptures say about him."

es.L: Pero {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que también Elías ha venido, y le hicieron cuanto quisieron, como está escrito de él».
es.B: Pero {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que Elías ya ha venido, y lo trataron como quisieron, tal como está escrito acerca de él».
es.R: Pero {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que Elías ya vino. Y la gente le hizo todo lo que quiso, tal como dicen las Escrituras acerca de él».

sw.L: Lakini nawaambia kwamba Eliya naye amekwisha kuja, nao wakamtendea walivyotaka, kama ilivyoandikwa kumhusu."
sw.B: Lakini nawaambia kwamba kwa kweli Eliya amekwisha kuja, nao walimtendea walivyopenda, kama ilivyoandikwa kumhusu."
sw.R: Lakini nawaambia, Eliya amekwisha kuja. Na watu walimfanyia kila walichotaka, kama vile Maandiko yanavyosema kumhusu."

decisions.choice: Elijah has come: John the Baptizer
decisions.reason: Mark does not name him here, but he has shown John dressed like Elijah (1:6; 2 Kings 1:8) and told how Herod killed him (6:17-29). Matthew 17:13 says the disciples understood he meant John.

decisions.choice: as it is written of him: what Scripture says of Elijah
alternatives: a prophecy of John by name
decisions.reason: Scripture tells how Jezebel sought Elijah's life (1 Kings 19:2, 10). What happened to John matches what Elijah suffered.

decisions.choice: they did: those who opposed him, Herod and Herodias in John's case
decisions.reason: The subject is not named.

decisions.choice: already; people
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that Elijah's coming is past and names the subject in general terms.

source.text: Καὶ ἐλθόντες πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς εἶδον ὄχλον πολὺν περὶ αὐτοὺς καὶ γραμματεῖς συζητοῦντας πρὸς αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: And having come to the disciples they saw a crowd great around them, and scribes arguing with them.

en.L: And when they came to the disciples, they saw a large crowd around them and scribes arguing with them.
en.B: When they got back to the other disciples, they found a large crowd surrounding them, and some scribes disputing with them.
en.R: When Jesus and the three came back to the other disciples, they saw a big crowd around them. Some teachers of God's law were arguing with them.

es.L: Y cuando llegaron adonde estaban los discípulos, vieron una gran multitud alrededor de ellos, y a unos escribas que discutían con ellos.
es.B: Cuando volvieron adonde estaban los otros discípulos, encontraron una gran multitud a su alrededor, y a algunos escribas que discutían con ellos.
es.R: Jesús y los tres volvieron adonde estaban los otros discípulos. Vieron mucha gente alrededor de ellos. Algunos maestros de la ley estaban discutiendo con ellos.

sw.L: Na walipofika kwa wanafunzi, waliona umati mkubwa wa watu ukiwazunguka, na waandishi wakijadiliana nao.
sw.B: Waliporudi kwa wanafunzi wengine, walikuta umati mkubwa wa watu umewazunguka, na baadhi ya waandishi wakibishana nao.
sw.R: Yesu na wale watatu walirudi kwa wanafunzi wengine. Waliona umati mkubwa wa watu umewazunguka. Baadhi ya walimu wa sheria walikuwa wakibishana nao.

decisions.choice: having come, they saw: plural, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts have the singular, making Jesus the one who saw. The SBLGNT reads the plural, which includes the three disciples. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the disciples: the others who had stayed below
decisions.reason: Jesus had taken only three up the mountain.

decisions.choice: arguing: disputing
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 9:10 and 8:11. Here it is a dispute, likely over the disciples' failure (9:18).

decisions.choice: the other disciples (B, R); Jesus and the three (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear which disciples are meant.

source.text: καὶ εὐθὺς πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἰδόντες αὐτὸν ἐξεθαμβήθησαν, καὶ προστρέχοντες ἠσπάζοντο αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And immediately all the crowd, having seen him, were greatly amazed, and running to [him] were greeting him.

en.L: And immediately all the crowd, when they saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, were greatly amazed, and running up, they greeted {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: As soon as the people saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, the whole crowd was overcome with wonder, and they ran up to greet {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: As soon as the people saw Jesus, they were very surprised. They all ran to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to welcome {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y en seguida toda la multitud, al verlo, quedó muy asombrada, y corriendo hacia {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} saludaban.
es.B: En cuanto la gente {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vio, toda la multitud quedó asombrada, y corrieron a saludarlo.
es.R: En cuanto la gente vio a Jesús, se sorprendió mucho. Todos corrieron hacia {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} para darle la bienvenida.

sw.L: Na mara moja umati wote, walipomwona, walishangaa sana, na wakimkimbilia, wakamsalimu.
sw.B: Mara watu walipomwona, umati wote ulijaa mshangao, nao wakamkimbilia ili kumsalimu.
sw.R: Mara watu walipomwona Yesu, walishangaa sana. Wote walimkimbilia ili kumkaribisha.

decisions.choice: greatly amazed: overcome with astonishment
decisions.reason: Mark uses this strong word only here and at 14:33 and 16:5-6.

decisions.choice: why they were amazed: Mark does not say
decisions.reason: Some suggest Jesus' face still showed the glory of the mountain, as Moses' face shone after Sinai (Exodus 34:29-30). Mark gives no reason; it may simply be his sudden arrival at the right moment.

decisions.choice: all the crowd ... having seen: plural forms with a singular crowd
decisions.reason: The crowd is thought of as many people, so the participles are plural.

decisions.choice: as soon as
decisions.reason: As in earlier chapters, Literal says "immediately" and the other levels vary the phrase.

source.text: καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτούς· Τί συζητεῖτε πρὸς αὑτούς;

records.literal_gloss: And he asked them, What are you disputing with them?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them, "What are you disputing with them?"
en.B: He asked them, "What are you arguing with them about?"
en.R: Jesus asked them, "What are you arguing with them about?"

es.L: Y les preguntó: «¿Qué {{plural_you:discuten|discutís}} con ellos?».
es.B: Les preguntó: «¿Sobre qué {{plural_you:están|estáis}} discutiendo con ellos?».
es.R: Jesús les preguntó: «¿Sobre qué {{plural_you:discuten|discutís}} con ellos?».

sw.L: Naye akawauliza, "Mnajadiliana nini nao?"
sw.B: Aliwauliza, "Mnabishana nao juu ya nini?"
sw.R: Yesu aliwauliza, "Mnabishana nao kuhusu nini?"

decisions.choice: them ... with them: Jesus asks the disciples what they are disputing with the scribes
alternatives: what are you disputing among yourselves
decisions.reason: The pronouns are not explained. Since the scribes were arguing with the disciples (9:14), Jesus most likely asks his disciples. Some manuscripts read the second pronoun as "among yourselves".

decisions.choice: disputing: the same verb as arguing in 9:14
decisions.reason: Jesus takes up the word Mark used for the scene.

decisions.choice: What are you arguing with them about?
alternatives: What are you disputing with them?
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the everyday verb and English word order.

source.text: καὶ ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ εἷς ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου· Διδάσκαλε, ἤνεγκα τὸν υἱόν μου πρὸς σέ, ἔχοντα πνεῦμα ἄλαλον·

records.literal_gloss: And answered him one out of the crowd, Teacher, I brought the son of me to you, having a spirit mute;

en.L: And one of the crowd answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, I brought my son to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, [because he] has a mute spirit;
en.B: A man in the crowd answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, I brought my son to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. He has a spirit that makes him unable to speak.
en.R: A man in the crowd answered, "Teacher, I brought my son to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. He has an evil spirit in him that keeps him from talking.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} respondió uno de la multitud: «Maestro, traje a mi hijo a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, [pues] tiene un espíritu mudo;
es.B: Uno de la multitud {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} respondió: «Maestro, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} he traído a mi hijo. Tiene un espíritu que no lo deja hablar.
es.R: Un hombre de la multitud respondió: «Maestro, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} traje a mi hijo. Tiene dentro un espíritu maligno que no lo deja hablar.

sw.L: Na mmoja wa umati akamjibu, "Mwalimu, nimemleta mwanangu {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}}, [kwa sababu] ana pepo bubu;
sw.B: Mtu mmoja katika umati alimjibu, "Mwalimu, nimemleta mwanangu {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}}. Ana pepo anayemfanya asiweze kusema.
sw.R: Mtu mmoja katika umati alijibu, "Mwalimu, nimemleta mwanangu {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}}. Ana pepo mbaya ndani yake anayemzuia asiongee.

decisions.choice: a mute spirit: a spirit that keeps him from speaking
alternatives: a spirit that does not speak
decisions.reason: The spirit is named by what it does to the boy. In 9:25 it is also called deaf.

decisions.choice: I brought my son to you: he came looking for Jesus
alternatives: he brought him to the disciples
decisions.reason: Jesus was on the mountain, so the father asked the disciples instead (9:18).

decisions.choice: one of the crowd: the man is not named
decisions.reason: He is simply a man in the crowd, a father (9:21).

decisions.choice: an evil spirit
decisions.reason: Readable uses "evil spirit", as in earlier chapters, and says what the spirit does.

decisions.choice: pepo bubu (L); pepo (B); pepo mbaya (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek says "spirit", meaning an evil spirit (meaning decision m1). "Roho" is also the word for the Holy Spirit and the human spirit, so Swahili says "pepo", as for the unclean spirit in verse 25; Readable adds "mbaya", as the English Readable says "evil spirit".

source.text: καὶ ὅπου ἐὰν αὐτὸν καταλάβῃ ῥήσσει αὐτόν, καὶ ἀφρίζει καὶ τρίζει τοὺς ὀδόντας καὶ ξηραίνεται· καὶ εἶπα τοῖς μαθηταῖς σου ἵνα αὐτὸ ἐκβάλωσιν, καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσαν.

records.literal_gloss: and whenever if him it seizes, it throws down him, and he foams and gnashes the teeth and is withering; and I spoke to the disciples of you that it they might cast out, and not they had power.

en.L: and wherever it seizes him, it throws him down, and he foams and grinds [his] teeth and becomes rigid; and I told {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples to cast it out, and they were not able."
en.B: Whenever it takes hold of him, it dashes him to the ground, and he foams at the mouth, grinds his teeth, and goes stiff. I asked {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples to throw it out, but they did not have the strength."
en.R: Whenever the spirit takes control of him, it throws him to the ground. Foam comes out of his mouth, he grinds his teeth, and his body becomes stiff. I asked {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} followers to force the spirit out, but they could not do it."

es.L: y dondequiera que se apodera de él, lo derriba, y echa espumarajos, y rechina los dientes, y se queda rígido; y dije a {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} discípulos que lo expulsaran, y no tuvieron fuerza».
es.B: Cada vez que se apodera de él, lo tira al suelo, y él echa espuma por la boca, rechina los dientes y se queda rígido. Les pedí a {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} discípulos que lo expulsaran, pero no tuvieron fuerza para hacerlo».
es.R: Cada vez que el espíritu se apodera de él, lo tira al suelo. Le sale espuma por la boca, rechina los dientes y su cuerpo se pone rígido. Les pedí a {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} discípulos que sacaran al espíritu, pero no pudieron».

sw.L: na popote anapomshika, humwangusha chini, naye hutokwa na povu, na kusaga meno, na kukakamaa; nami niliwaambia wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wamtoe, nao hawakuweza."
sw.B: Kila anapomshika, humtupa chini, naye hutoa povu kinywani, husaga meno, na mwili wake hukakamaa. Niliwaomba wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wamtoe yule pepo, lakini hawakuwa na nguvu ya kufanya hivyo."
sw.R: Kila mara pepo huyo anapomshika, humwangusha chini. Povu hutoka kinywani mwake, husaga meno, na mwili wake hukakamaa. Niliwaomba wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wamfukuze pepo huyo, lakini hawakuweza."

decisions.choice: becomes rigid: goes stiff during the attack
decisions.reason: The verb means to dry up or wither. In this list of what happens in an attack it most likely means the body goes stiff. It could mean he is wasting away.

decisions.choice: the attacks: like what is now called an epileptic seizure
decisions.reason: The signs are those of a seizure. Mark tells it as the work of a spirit, and Jesus deals with it as one (9:25). Matthew 17:15 also describes the boy's fits.

decisions.choice: wherever: at any place and time
decisions.reason: The word means where, but with "if" it covers every occasion.

decisions.choice: they were not able: they lacked the strength
decisions.reason: The verb means to have strength. The disciples had driven out spirits before (6:13) but failed here.

decisions.choice: foams at the mouth (B); foam comes out of his mouth (R)
decisions.reason: English needs "mouth" with this verb.

decisions.choice: discípulos (every level)
decisions.reason: The New Testament choice for Spanish keeps "discípulos" at Readable too, where the English Readable says "followers". The same in verses 28, 30 and 33.

decisions.choice: kukakamaa (L); hukakamaa (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb means "dries up, withers", here the body going stiff in the attack (meaning decision m1). "Kukauka" would say only that he dried up; "kukakamaa" says that he goes rigid.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτοῖς λέγει· Ὦ γενεὰ ἄπιστος, ἕως πότε πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἔσομαι;

records.literal_gloss: And answering them he says, O generation unbelieving, until when with you will I be?

en.L: And answering them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says, "O unbelieving generation, how long will I be with you?
en.B: Jesus answered them, "You unbelieving generation! How long must I stay with you?
en.R: Jesus said to them, "You people do not believe! How long do I have to stay with you?

es.L: Y respondiéndoles, dice: «¡Oh generación incrédula! ¿Hasta cuándo estaré con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?
es.B: Jesús les respondió: «¡Generación incrédula! ¿Hasta cuándo tendré que quedarme con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «¡{{plural_you:Ustedes no creen|Vosotros no creéis}}! ¿Hasta cuándo tendré que estar con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?

sw.L: Naye akawajibu, anasema, "Ewe kizazi kisichoamini, nitakuwa pamoja nanyi mpaka lini?
sw.B: Yesu aliwajibu, "Enyi kizazi kisichoamini! Nitakaa nanyi mpaka lini?
sw.R: Yesu aliwaambia, "Ninyi watu hamwamini! Itanibidi nikae nanyi mpaka lini?

decisions.choice: them: the whole company, disciples, father, crowd and scribes
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to all of them. The word "generation" takes in the people of his time, the disciples included, since they failed (9:18).

decisions.choice: unbelieving generation: Israel's lack of faith in the wilderness
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 32:5 and 32:20 speak of a crooked generation, children without faithfulness. As Moses came down Sinai to find unfaithfulness (Exodus 32), Jesus comes down to find unbelief.

decisions.choice: unbelieving: without trust in God
decisions.reason: The word is the opposite of believing. It points ahead to the father's words in 9:24.

decisions.choice: says: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Another of Mark's vivid presents. The sense is past.

decisions.choice: You people do not believe!
decisions.reason: Readable turns the address into a plain statement.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the whole company there, disciples, father, crowd and scribes (meaning decision m1), so every plural "you" and its verb in verse 19 is the reader setting: ustedes forms (the default) or vosotros forms.

source.text: ἕως πότε ἀνέξομαι ὑμῶν;

records.literal_gloss: Until when will I bear with you?

en.L: How long will I put up with you?
en.B: How long must I bear with you?
en.R: How long must I be patient with you?

es.L: ¿Hasta cuándo {{plural_you:los|os}} soportaré?
es.B: ¿Hasta cuándo tendré que {{plural_you:aguantarlos|aguantaros}}?
es.R: ¿Hasta cuándo tendré que tener paciencia con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?

sw.L: Nitawavumilia mpaka lini?
sw.B: Nitawachukulia mpaka lini?
sw.R: Itanibidi niwe na subira nanyi mpaka lini?

decisions.choice: until when: how long
decisions.reason: A plain question of time, spoken in sorrow.

decisions.choice: bear with: put up with, endure patiently
decisions.reason: The verb means to hold up under something hard.

decisions.choice: be patient with
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday phrase.

source.text: φέρετε αὐτὸν πρός με.

records.literal_gloss: Bring him to me.

en.L: Bring him to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.B: Bring the boy to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.R: Bring the boy to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

es.L: {{plural_you:Tráiganlo|Traedlo}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}».
es.B: {{plural_you:Tráiganme|Traedme}} al muchacho».
es.R: {{plural_you:Tráiganme|Traedme}} aquí al muchacho».

sw.L: Mleteni {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}."
sw.B: Mleteni kijana {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}."
sw.R: Mleteni mtoto huyo {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}."

decisions.choice: bring: a plural command, said to those standing there
decisions.reason: The command is plural. In 9:20 several people bring the boy.

decisions.choice: the boy
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the son so the pronoun is not taken for Jesus.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:Tráiganme|Traedme}}, with no deity_pronoun span on "me"
decisions.reason: The command is plural, said to those standing there (meaning decision m1), so it takes the plural_you setting. Spanish joins "me" to the command, so there is no separate word to capitalise; Literal says "a mí", which takes the span.

source.text: καὶ ἤνεγκαν αὐτὸν πρὸς αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And they brought him to him.

en.L: And they brought him to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: So they brought the boy to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: So they brought the boy to Jesus.

es.L: Y lo trajeron a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Entonces llevaron al muchacho ante {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Entonces llevaron al muchacho ante Jesús.

sw.L: Nao wakamleta {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}.
sw.B: Basi walimleta kijana {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}.
sw.R: Basi walimleta kijana kwa Yesu.

decisions.choice: him to him: the boy to Jesus
decisions.reason: The first pronoun is the boy, the second Jesus.

decisions.choice: the boy (B, R); Jesus (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the people.

source.text: καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὸν τὸ πνεῦμα εὐθὺς συνεσπάραξεν αὐτόν, καὶ πεσὼν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἐκυλίετο ἀφρίζων.

records.literal_gloss: And having seen him, the spirit immediately threw into convulsions him, and having fallen on the ground he was rolling around, foaming.

en.L: And when the spirit saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, it immediately threw him into convulsions, and falling on the ground, he rolled around, foaming.
en.B: As soon as the spirit saw Jesus, it threw the boy into a fit. He fell to the ground and rolled about, foaming at the mouth.
en.R: When the evil spirit saw Jesus, right away it made the boy shake violently. The boy fell on the ground. He rolled around, and foam came out of his mouth.

es.L: Y cuando el espíritu {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vio, en seguida sacudió al muchacho con convulsiones, y cayendo en tierra, se revolcaba echando espumarajos.
es.B: En cuanto el espíritu vio a Jesús, le provocó al muchacho un ataque violento. El muchacho cayó al suelo y se revolcaba echando espuma por la boca.
es.R: Cuando el espíritu maligno vio a Jesús, en seguida hizo que el muchacho se sacudiera con violencia. El muchacho cayó al suelo. Se revolcaba, y le salía espuma por la boca.

sw.L: Na yule pepo alipomwona, mara akamtikisa kwa nguvu, naye akianguka chini, akawa akigaagaa, akitokwa na povu.
sw.B: Mara pepo alipomwona Yesu, alimtia kijana kifafa. Kijana akaanguka chini, akagaagaa huku akitoa povu kinywani.
sw.R: Pepo mbaya alipomwona Yesu, mara moja alimfanya kijana atetemeke vibaya. Kijana akaanguka chini. Akagaagaa, na povu likatoka kinywani mwake.

decisions.choice: having seen him: the spirit saw Jesus
decisions.reason: The participle is masculine though "spirit" is neuter. It is joined to the spirit by sense, as a person. It could be read of the boy, but the spirit is the subject of the main verb.

decisions.choice: threw into convulsions: shook him violently
decisions.reason: The verb means to tear or shake about. It describes the seizure.

decisions.choice: was rolling around: went on rolling about
decisions.reason: The imperfect describes continuing movement.

decisions.choice: Jesus; the boy
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who is meant by each pronoun.

decisions.choice: sacudió al muchacho
decisions.reason: With "lo" already standing for Jesus, a second "lo" for the boy would be unclear in Spanish, so Literal names the boy, as the English Balanced does; the spirit saw Jesus (meaning decision m1).

source.text: καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ· Πόσος χρόνος ἐστὶν ὡς τοῦτο γέγονεν αὐτῷ;

records.literal_gloss: And he asked the father of him, How long a time is it that this has been with him?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked his father, "How long a time is it since this has happened to him?"
en.B: Jesus asked the boy's father, "Since when has this been happening to him?"
en.R: Jesus asked the boy's father, "When did this start happening to your son?"

es.L: Y preguntó a su padre: «¿Cuánto tiempo hace que le sucede esto?».
es.B: Jesús preguntó al padre del muchacho: «¿Desde cuándo le pasa esto?».
es.R: Jesús le preguntó al padre del muchacho: «¿Cuándo empezó a pasarle esto a tu hijo?».

sw.L: Naye akamwuliza baba yake, "Ni muda gani tangu haya yampate?"
sw.B: Yesu alimwuliza baba wa kijana, "Hali hii imekuwa ikimpata tangu lini?"
sw.R: Yesu alimwuliza baba wa kijana, "Mwanao alianza kupatwa na hali hii lini?"

decisions.choice: his father: the boy's father
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers to the boy.

decisions.choice: this: the attacks
decisions.reason: Jesus asks how long the boy has suffered.

decisions.choice: the boy's father
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear whose father is meant.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ἐκ παιδιόθεν·

records.literal_gloss: And he said, From childhood;

en.L: And he said, "From childhood;
en.B: He answered, "Since he was a small child.
en.R: The father said, "Since he was a little boy.

es.L: Y él dijo: «Desde niño;
es.B: Él respondió: «Desde que era muy pequeño.
es.R: El padre dijo: «Desde que era un niño pequeño.

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Tangu utotoni;
sw.B: Akajibu, "Tangu alipokuwa mtoto mdogo.
sw.R: Baba yake akasema, "Tangu alipokuwa mvulana mdogo.

decisions.choice: from childhood: since he was very young
decisions.reason: The word points to early childhood. The boy is still a child (9:24).

decisions.choice: The father
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker.

source.text: καὶ πολλάκις καὶ εἰς πῦρ αὐτὸν ἔβαλεν καὶ εἰς ὕδατα ἵνα ἀπολέσῃ αὐτόν· ἀλλ’ εἴ τι δύνῃ, βοήθησον ἡμῖν σπλαγχνισθεὶς ἐφ’ ἡμᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: and often both into fire him it cast and into waters, that it might destroy him; but if anything you are able, help us, having compassion on us.

en.L: and often it has thrown him both into fire and into water, to destroy him; but if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are able [to do] anything, help us, having compassion on us."
en.B: Many times it has thrown him into fire or into water to kill him. But if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are able to do anything at all, help us. Have pity on us!"
en.R: The spirit has often thrown him into fire or into water to try to kill him. If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can do anything, please feel sorry for us and help us!"

es.L: y muchas veces lo ha arrojado tanto al fuego como al agua para destruirlo; pero si algo puedes, ayúdanos, teniendo compasión de nosotros».
es.B: Muchas veces lo ha arrojado al fuego o al agua para matarlo. Pero si puedes hacer algo, ayúdanos. ¡Ten compasión de nosotros!».
es.R: El espíritu muchas veces lo ha tirado al fuego o al agua para intentar matarlo. Si puedes hacer algo, por favor, ten compasión de nosotros y ayúdanos».

sw.L: na mara nyingi amemtupa motoni na majini ili amwangamize; lakini ukiweza kufanya lolote, utusaidie, ukituonea huruma."
sw.B: Mara nyingi amemtupa motoni au majini ili amuue. Lakini kama unaweza kufanya lolote, tusaidie. Tuonee huruma!"
sw.R: Pepo huyo mara nyingi amemtupa motoni au majini ili ajaribu kumuua. Kama unaweza kufanya kitu chochote, tafadhali tuonee huruma, utusaidie!"

decisions.choice: has thrown: the spirit has done this again and again
decisions.reason: "Often" shows that the past tense sums up many attacks.

decisions.choice: if you are able: the father is not sure Jesus can help
decisions.reason: After the disciples failed, the father doubts. Jesus takes up these words in 9:23.

decisions.choice: having compassion: deep pity
decisions.reason: The verb speaks of feeling stirred within. Mark uses it of Jesus himself (1:41; 6:34; 8:2).

decisions.choice: us: the father counts himself with his son
decisions.reason: The father shares his son's suffering and asks for both of them.

decisions.choice: the spirit; to try to
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject and shows that the spirit's aim had not succeeded.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Τὸ Εἰ δύνῃ, πάντα δυνατὰ τῷ πιστεύοντι.

records.literal_gloss: And Jesus said to him, The If you are able! All things are possible to the [one] believing.

en.L: And Jesus said to him, "'If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are able!' All things [are] possible for the one who believes."
en.B: Jesus said to him, "'If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can!' All things are possible for the one who believes."
en.R: Jesus said to him, "Why do you say, 'If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can'? Everything is possible for a person who believes."

es.L: Y Jesús le dijo: «“¡Si puedes!”. Todo [es] posible para el que cree».
es.B: Jesús le dijo: «“¡Si puedes!”. Todo es posible para el que cree».
es.R: Jesús le dijo: «¿Por qué dices “si puedes”? Todo es posible para quien cree».

sw.L: Na Yesu akamwambia, "'Ukiweza!' Mambo yote yanawezekana kwa yeye aaminiye."
sw.B: Yesu alimwambia, "'Kama unaweza!' Mambo yote yanawezekana kwa mtu anayeamini."
sw.R: Yesu alimwambia, "Kwa nini unasema, 'Kama unaweza'? Kila kitu kinawezekana kwa mtu anayeamini."

decisions.choice: 'If you are able!': Jesus repeats the father's words and throws them back
alternatives: Jesus asks if he himself is able
decisions.reason: The article points to the father's phrase as a quotation. The question is not whether Jesus is able but whether the father will trust.

decisions.choice: 'If you are able!', the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: If you are able to believe, all things are possible
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "to believe", which smooths the grammar and makes it a condition placed on the father. The shorter reading is found in the earliest manuscripts. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the one who believes: the father, who answers in 9:24
alternatives: Jesus himself, whose trust in God makes all things possible
decisions.reason: The father replies "I believe", so he takes the words to mean him. Some see Jesus' own trust in God in them too. The two are not exclusive.

decisions.choice: believes: trusts God and his power at work in Jesus
decisions.reason: Believing in Mark is trust that God will act (5:36; 11:22-24).

decisions.choice: Why do you say
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that Jesus is quoting the father.

source.text: εὐθὺς κράξας ὁ πατὴρ τοῦ παιδίου ἔλεγεν· Πιστεύω· βοήθει μου τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ.

records.literal_gloss: Immediately having cried out the father of the child was saying, I believe; help of me the unbelief.

en.L: Immediately the father of the child cried out and said, "I believe; help my unbelief!"
en.B: At once the boy's father cried out, "I believe! Help my unbelief!"
en.R: Right away the boy's father shouted, "I do believe! Help me with my unbelief!"

es.L: En seguida, gritando, el padre del niño decía: «Creo; ayuda a mi incredulidad».
es.B: Al instante el padre del muchacho exclamó: «¡Creo! ¡Ayuda a mi incredulidad!».
es.R: En seguida el padre del muchacho gritó: «¡Sí creo! ¡Ayúdame en mi falta de fe!».

sw.L: Mara moja baba wa mtoto akipiga kelele alikuwa akisema, "Naamini; nisaidie kutokuamini kwangu!"
sw.B: Mara baba wa kijana alipaza sauti, "Ninaamini! Nisaidie kutokuamini kwangu!"
sw.R: Mara moja baba wa kijana alipiga kelele, "Kweli ninaamini! Nisaidie katika kutokuamini kwangu!"

decisions.choice: cried out, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "with tears" and address Jesus as "Lord". The earliest manuscripts lack both. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: help my unbelief: help me where my faith falls short
decisions.reason: The father admits that his trust is mixed with doubt and asks Jesus to help him in that weakness.

decisions.choice: believe, unbelief: the same word family as 9:19 and 9:23
decisions.reason: Believing and unbelief are set side by side in one man.

decisions.choice: Help me with my unbelief
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the father asks help for himself.

source.text: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι ἐπισυντρέχει ὄχλος ἐπετίμησεν τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἀκαθάρτῳ λέγων αὐτῷ· Τὸ ἄλαλον καὶ κωφὸν πνεῦμα, ἐγὼ ἐπιτάσσω σοι, ἔξελθε ἐξ αὐτοῦ καὶ μηκέτι εἰσέλθῃς εἰς αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Having seen now Jesus that was running together a crowd, he rebuked the spirit, the unclean, saying to it, Mute and deaf spirit, I command you, come out of him and no more may you enter into him.

en.L: Now when Jesus saw that a crowd was running together, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it, "Mute and deaf spirit, I command you, come out of him and never enter him again."
en.B: When Jesus saw that a crowd was quickly gathering, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave the unclean spirit a stern order: "You mute and deaf spirit, I command you to come out of him and never go into him again!"
en.R: Jesus saw that more people were running over to see. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke sternly to the evil spirit. "You spirit that makes this boy deaf and unable to speak," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "I order you to come out of him! Never go back into him again!"

es.L: Y viendo Jesús que la multitud se agolpaba, reprendió al espíritu impuro, diciéndole: «Espíritu mudo y sordo, yo te ordeno: sal de él y no entres más en él».
es.B: Cuando Jesús vio que la multitud se juntaba rápidamente, dio una orden severa al espíritu impuro: «Espíritu mudo y sordo, yo te ordeno que salgas de él y que nunca más vuelvas a entrar en él».
es.R: Jesús vio que más gente llegaba corriendo para ver. Entonces habló con severidad al espíritu maligno: «Espíritu que haces que este muchacho sea sordo y no pueda hablar —le dijo—, yo te ordeno que salgas de él. ¡No vuelvas a entrar en él nunca más!».

sw.L: Na Yesu alipoona kwamba umati unakusanyika mbio, alimkemea yule pepo mchafu, akimwambia, "Wewe pepo bubu na kiziwi, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninakuamuru, mtoke, wala usimwingie tena."
sw.B: Yesu alipoona kwamba umati wa watu ulikuwa ukikusanyika upesi, alimwamuru yule pepo mchafu kwa ukali, akisema, "Wewe pepo bubu na kiziwi, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninakuamuru umtoke, wala usimwingie tena kamwe!"
sw.R: Yesu aliona kwamba watu wengi zaidi walikuwa wakija mbio kuona. Kwa hiyo alimkemea yule pepo mbaya kwa ukali. Akasema, "Wewe pepo unayemfanya kijana huyu kuwa kiziwi na asiweze kusema, ninakuamuru umtoke! Usimwingie tena kamwe!"

decisions.choice: a crowd was running together: more people were gathering
decisions.reason: The word suggests people running up to join. Jesus acts before a larger crowd forms.

decisions.choice: rebuked: commanded sternly
decisions.reason: The same verb Jesus uses with spirits and with the storm (1:25; 4:39).

decisions.choice: I: emphatic, I myself command you
decisions.reason: Jesus stresses his own authority, where the disciples had failed.

decisions.choice: never enter him again: the cure is permanent
decisions.reason: The command shuts the spirit out for good, since its attacks had come and gone (9:18).

decisions.choice: You spirit that makes this boy deaf and unable to speak
decisions.reason: Readable says what the spirit's name means.

decisions.choice: espíritu impuro (L, B); espíritu maligno (R)
decisions.reason: The New Testament choice for Spanish: "impuro" says the spirit is unclean before God; "inmundo" is older and now sounds like plain dirt. Readable says "maligno", as the English Readable says "evil spirit".

decisions.choice: pepo mchafu (L, B); pepo mbaya (R)
decisions.reason: The New Testament choice for Swahili: "pepo mchafu" says the spirit is unclean before God; Readable says "pepo mbaya", as the English Readable says "evil spirit". "Roho" is kept for the Holy Spirit and the human spirit.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninakuamuru
decisions.reason: The Greek "I" is emphatic (meaning decision m3), so Swahili writes the free pronoun "mimi". English never puts "I" under the setting, but the Swahili style gives the span to every free pronoun by which Jesus speaks of himself.

source.text: καὶ κράξας καὶ πολλὰ σπαράξας ἐξῆλθεν· καὶ ἐγένετο ὡσεὶ νεκρὸς ὥστε τοὺς πολλοὺς λέγειν ὅτι ἀπέθανεν.

records.literal_gloss: And having cried out and much having convulsed [him], it came out; and he became as if dead, so that the many said that he died.

en.L: And after crying out and convulsing [him] greatly, it came out; and he became like [one] dead, so that the many said, "He has died."
en.B: The spirit shrieked, threw him into violent convulsions, and came out. The boy was left lying like a corpse, so that most of them said, "He has died."
en.R: The spirit screamed and shook the boy hard. Then it came out of him. The boy looked as if he were dead, and many people said, "He is dead."

es.L: Y gritando y sacudiéndolo con violencia, salió; y quedó como muerto, de modo que los más decían: «Ha muerto».
es.B: El espíritu dio un alarido, lo sacudió con violentas convulsiones y salió. El muchacho quedó tendido como un cadáver, de modo que la mayoría decía: «Ha muerto».
es.R: El espíritu gritó y sacudió con fuerza al muchacho. Luego salió de él. El muchacho parecía muerto, y mucha gente decía: «Está muerto».

sw.L: Na akipiga kelele na kumtikisa sana, akatoka; naye akawa kama mfu, hata wengi wakasema, "Amekufa."
sw.B: Yule pepo alipiga yowe, akamtia kifafa kikali, akamtoka. Kijana akabaki amelala kama maiti, hata wengi wao wakasema, "Amekufa."
sw.R: Pepo huyo alipiga kelele, akamtikisa kijana kwa nguvu. Kisha akamtoka. Kijana alionekana kama aliyekufa, na watu wengi wakasema, "Amekufa."

decisions.choice: having cried out, having convulsed: the spirit is the subject
decisions.reason: The participles are masculine, as in 9:20, but they go with the spirit that comes out.

decisions.choice: the many: most of those there
decisions.reason: With the article the phrase means the majority.

decisions.choice: crying out: a shriek without words
decisions.reason: The spirit had made the boy mute, and no words are reported.

decisions.choice: like a corpse
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a vivid phrase for the boy's lifeless look.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς κρατήσας τῆς χειρὸς αὐτοῦ ἤγειρεν αὐτόν, καὶ ἀνέστη.

records.literal_gloss: But Jesus having taken the hand of him raised him, and he arose.

en.L: But Jesus took him by the hand and raised him, and he arose.
en.B: But Jesus took hold of his hand and lifted him up, and he got to his feet.
en.R: But Jesus took the boy by the hand and helped him up. And the boy stood up.

es.L: Pero Jesús, tomándolo de la mano, lo levantó, y se levantó.
es.B: Pero Jesús lo tomó de la mano y lo levantó, y él se puso de pie.
es.R: Pero Jesús tomó al muchacho de la mano y lo ayudó a levantarse. Y el muchacho se puso de pie.

sw.L: Lakini Yesu akamshika mkono, akamwinua, naye akainuka.
sw.B: Lakini Yesu alimshika mkono, akamwinua, naye akasimama.
sw.R: Lakini Yesu alimshika kijana mkono, akamsaidia kuinuka. Kijana akasimama.

decisions.choice: raised, arose: the verbs used for resurrection
decisions.reason: The same verbs describe rising from the dead (5:41-42; 9:9-10). The boy seemed dead, and Jesus raises him.

decisions.choice: but: in contrast to those who said he was dead
decisions.reason: The small word sets Jesus' act against the crowd's verdict.

decisions.choice: lifted him up, got to his feet (B); helped him up, stood up (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use everyday words. Literal keeps the words that recall resurrection.

source.text: καὶ εἰσελθόντος αὐτοῦ εἰς οἶκον οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ κατ’ ἰδίαν ἐπηρώτων αὐτόν· Ὅτι ἡμεῖς οὐκ ἠδυνήθημεν ἐκβαλεῖν αὐτό;

records.literal_gloss: And having entered he into a house, the disciples of him in private were asking him, Why we not were able to cast out it?

en.L: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had gone into a house, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples were asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} privately, "Why were we not able to cast it out?"
en.B: After {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went indoors, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} privately, "Why could we not throw it out?"
en.R: Later Jesus went into a house. When {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers were alone with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they asked, "Why could we not force the spirit out?"

es.L: Y cuando entró en una casa, {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaban en privado: «¿Por qué nosotros no pudimos expulsarlo?».
es.B: Cuando entró en casa, {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaron a solas: «¿Por qué no pudimos nosotros expulsarlo?».
es.R: Más tarde, Jesús entró en una casa. Cuando {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos estuvieron a solas con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaron: «¿Por qué no pudimos nosotros sacar al espíritu?».

sw.L: Na alipoingia nyumbani, wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wakamwuliza faraghani, "Mbona sisi hatukuweza kumtoa?"
sw.B: Alipoingia ndani ya nyumba, wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walimwuliza faraghani, "Kwa nini sisi hatukuweza kumfukuza?"
sw.R: Baadaye Yesu aliingia ndani ya nyumba. Wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walipokuwa peke yao pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}, walimwuliza, "Kwa nini sisi hatukuweza kumfukuza yule pepo?"

decisions.choice: why: the small word opens a question
alternatives: that: we could not cast it out
decisions.reason: As in 9:11, the word introduces a question here.

decisions.choice: we: emphatic, we ourselves
decisions.reason: They had driven out demons before (6:13) and are puzzled that they failed.

decisions.choice: a house: a place for private teaching
decisions.reason: Mark often has Jesus explain things to the disciples alone in a house (7:17; 10:10).

decisions.choice: throw out (B); force out (R)
decisions.reason: The same pattern as in earlier chapters.

source.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τοῦτο τὸ γένος ἐν οὐδενὶ δύναται ἐξελθεῖν εἰ μὴ ἐν προσευχῇ.

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, This kind by nothing is able to go out except by prayer.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "This kind is not able to come out by anything except by prayer."
en.B: He told them, "This kind cannot be made to come out by any means except prayer."
en.R: Jesus answered, "Only prayer can make this kind of spirit come out."

es.L: Y les dijo: «Esta clase no puede salir con nada, sino con oración».
es.B: Les respondió: «Esta clase no puede salir por ningún medio, sino con la oración».
es.R: Jesús respondió: «Solo la oración puede hacer salir a esta clase de espíritu».

sw.L: Naye akawaambia, "Aina hii haiwezi kutoka kwa kitu chochote isipokuwa kwa maombi."
sw.B: Aliwaambia, "Aina hii haiwezi kutolewa kwa njia yoyote ila kwa maombi."
sw.R: Yesu akajibu, "Ni maombi peke yake yanayoweza kumtoa pepo wa aina hii."

decisions.choice: by prayer, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "and fasting". The earliest manuscripts lack it. The addition may reflect the growing practice of fasting in the church. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: this kind: this kind of spirit
decisions.reason: Jesus means the kind of spirit that held the boy.

decisions.choice: by prayer: by depending on God
alternatives: by a special prayer said over the boy
decisions.reason: Jesus does not pray aloud in the story. He speaks of the trust in God that prayer expresses, which the disciples lacked (9:19). The words do not explain why this kind needs it more than others.

decisions.choice: this kind of spirit
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind is meant.

source.text: Κἀκεῖθεν ἐξελθόντες παρεπορεύοντο διὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας, καὶ οὐκ ἤθελεν ἵνα τις γνοῖ·

records.literal_gloss: And from there having gone out they were passing through Galilee, and not did he want that anyone should know;

en.L: And going out from there, they were passing through Galilee, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not want anyone to know [it];
en.B: They left that place and made their way through Galilee. Jesus did not want anyone to know where they were,
en.R: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers left that area and traveled through Galilee. Jesus did not want people to know where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was,

es.L: Y saliendo de allí, iban pasando por Galilea, y no quería que nadie [lo] supiera;
es.B: Se fueron de allí y atravesaron Galilea. Jesús no quería que nadie supiera dónde estaban,
es.R: Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos salieron de aquella región y viajaron por Galilea. Jesús no quería que la gente supiera dónde estaba,

sw.L: Na wakitoka huko, walikuwa wakipita katikati ya Galilaya, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} hakutaka mtu yeyote ajue;
sw.B: Waliondoka mahali hapo, wakapita katika Galilaya. Yesu hakutaka mtu yeyote ajue mahali walipokuwa,
sw.R: Yesu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} waliondoka sehemu ile, wakasafiri katika Galilaya. Yesu hakutaka watu wajue mahali alipokuwa,

decisions.choice: passing through: traveling through without stopping to teach the crowds
decisions.reason: The verb means to go along through a place. The journey now leads toward Jerusalem (10:1, 10:32).

decisions.choice: he did not want anyone to know: because he was teaching the disciples
decisions.reason: The next sentence gives the reason: this was a time to teach the Twelve.

decisions.choice: where they were (B); where he was (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what Jesus did not want known.

source.text: ἐδίδασκεν γὰρ τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς ὅτι Ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοται εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων, καὶ ἀποκτενοῦσιν αὐτόν, καὶ ἀποκτανθεὶς μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἀναστήσεται.

records.literal_gloss: he was teaching for the disciples of him and he was saying to them that, The Son of Man is handed over into [the] hands of men, and they will kill him, and having been killed after three days he will arise.

en.L: for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and saying to them, "The Son of Man is handed over into [the] hands of {{gender:people|men}}, and they will kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has been killed, after three days {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rise."
en.B: for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was busy teaching {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples. "The Son of Man is going to be handed over into human hands," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told them. "They will kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and three days after {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is killed {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rise again."
