en.R: because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers. He said to them, "The Son of Man will be handed over to people who will kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But three days after {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} dies, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will come back to life."

es.L: pues enseñaba a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos y les decía: «El Hijo del Hombre es entregado en manos de {{gender:seres humanos|hombres}}, y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} matarán, y una vez muerto, después de tres días resucitará».
es.B: porque estaba ocupado enseñando a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos. «El Hijo del Hombre va a ser entregado en manos humanas —les decía—. Lo matarán, y tres días después de muerto resucitará».
es.R: porque estaba enseñando a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos. Les dijo: «El Hijo del Hombre será entregado a gente que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} matará. Pero tres días después de morir, volverá a la vida».

sw.L: kwa maana alikuwa akiwafundisha wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, na kuwaambia kwamba, "Mwana wa Adamu anatolewa mikononi mwa wanadamu, nao watamuua, na akiisha kuuawa, baada ya siku tatu atafufuka."
sw.B: kwa sababu alikuwa akishughulika kuwafundisha wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Aliwaambia, "Mwana wa Adamu atatolewa mikononi mwa wanadamu. Watamuua, na siku tatu baada ya kuuawa atafufuka."
sw.R: kwa sababu alikuwa akiwafundisha wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Aliwaambia, "Mwana wa Adamu atakabidhiwa kwa watu watakaomuua. Lakini siku tatu baada ya kufa, atarudi kuwa hai."

decisions.choice: is handed over: a present tense for something certain and already under way
alternatives: it is happening at this moment
decisions.reason: The present makes the future sure. The verbs that follow are future.

decisions.choice: handed over: delivered up to others
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of Judas handing Jesus over (3:19; 14:10) and of God giving up his servant (Isaiah 53:6 in the Greek). Here the one who hands him over is not named.

decisions.choice: after three days: on the third day
decisions.reason: As in 8:31, the phrase counts parts of days. Mark tells of the rising early on the third day (16:1-2).

decisions.choice: Son of Man ... hands of men: a play on the word for human beings
decisions.reason: The one called the Son of Man is given into the hands of human beings.

decisions.choice: handed over
decisions.reason: All levels say "handed over", since Jesus does not yet speak of Judas and the verb is wider than betrayal.

decisions.choice: el Hijo del Hombre ... {{gender:seres humanos|hombres}} (L); manos humanas (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek plays on "the Son of Man" and "men" (meaning decision m4). "Seres humanos" and "humanas" keep the link with "Hombre" in the sense of humankind, and the traditional "hombres" of the setting keeps the very word, as in Matthew 17:22.

decisions.choice: Mwana wa Adamu ... wanadamu
decisions.reason: The Greek plays on "the Son of Man" and "men" (meaning decision m4). "Wanadamu" (human beings) echoes "Adamu" in the title, so Literal and Balanced keep the play, as in Matthew 17:22. Swahili needs no gender span: "wanadamu" already means men and women.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἠγνόουν τὸ ῥῆμα, καὶ ἐφοβοῦντο αὐτὸν ἐπερωτῆσαι.

records.literal_gloss: But they did not understand the saying, and they were afraid him to ask.

en.L: But they did not understand the saying, and they were afraid to ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: But they did not grasp what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} meant, and they were afraid to question {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: But the disciples did not understand what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} meant, and they were too afraid to ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Pero ellos no entendían el dicho, y temían preguntarle.
es.B: Pero ellos no comprendían lo que quería decir, y tenían miedo de hacerle preguntas.
es.R: Pero los discípulos no entendieron lo que quería decir, y tenían demasiado miedo para preguntarle.

sw.L: Lakini wao hawakulielewa neno hilo, nao waliogopa kumwuliza.
sw.B: Lakini hawakuelewa alichomaanisha, nao waliogopa kumwuliza.
sw.R: Lakini wanafunzi hawakuelewa alichomaanisha, nao waliogopa sana kumwuliza.

decisions.choice: did not understand, were afraid: imperfects, a lasting state
decisions.reason: They went on not understanding and went on being afraid.

decisions.choice: afraid to ask: perhaps afraid of the answer, or of a rebuke like Peter's (8:33)
decisions.reason: Mark does not say why. The last time a disciple questioned this teaching, Jesus rebuked him.

decisions.choice: what he meant
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what they did not understand.

source.text: Καὶ ἦλθον εἰς Καφαρναούμ.

records.literal_gloss: And they came to Capernaum.

en.L: And they came to Capernaum.
en.B: They arrived at Capernaum.
en.R: Then they came to the town of Capernaum.

es.L: Y llegaron a Cafarnaúm.
es.B: Llegaron a Cafarnaúm.
es.R: Luego llegaron al pueblo de Cafarnaúm.

sw.L: Na wakafika Kapernaumu.
sw.B: Walifika Kapernaumu.
sw.R: Kisha walifika katika mji wa Kapernaumu.

decisions.choice: Capernaum: Jesus' base by the lake
decisions.reason: Jesus had made his home there (1:21; 2:1).

decisions.choice: the town of
decisions.reason: Readable says what Capernaum was.

source.text: καὶ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ γενόμενος ἐπηρώτα αὐτούς· Τί ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ διελογίζεσθε;

records.literal_gloss: And in the house having been, he was asking them, What on the way were you discussing?

en.L: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was in the house, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them, "What were you discussing on the way?"
en.B: Once they were inside the house, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them, "What was it you were debating as we walked?"
en.R: When they were inside the house, Jesus asked {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers, "What were you talking about while we were walking?"

es.L: Y estando en la casa, les preguntaba: «¿Qué {{plural_you:discutían|discutíais}} en el camino?».
es.B: Una vez dentro de la casa, les preguntó: «¿Qué era lo que {{plural_you:debatían|debatíais}} mientras caminábamos?».
es.R: Cuando ya estaban dentro de la casa, Jesús preguntó a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos: «¿De qué {{plural_you:hablaban|hablabais}} mientras íbamos caminando?».

sw.L: Na alipokuwa ndani ya nyumba, akawauliza, "Mlikuwa mkijadiliana nini njiani?"
sw.B: Walipokuwa ndani ya nyumba, aliwauliza, "Mlikuwa mkibishana juu ya nini tulipokuwa tukitembea?"
sw.R: Walipokuwa ndani ya nyumba, Yesu aliwauliza wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, "Mlikuwa mkiongea nini tulipokuwa tukitembea?"

decisions.choice: the house: a house known to the reader, perhaps Peter's
decisions.reason: The article points to a known house. Simon's house in Capernaum appears in 1:29 and perhaps 2:1.

decisions.choice: discussing: reasoning together, debating
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 8:16-17. The next sentence shows what the debate was.

decisions.choice: the way: the road they traveled
decisions.reason: The word means road. Mark often places teaching "on the way" to Jerusalem (8:27; 10:32).

decisions.choice: What was it you were debating as we walked? (B); while we were walking (R)
alternatives: What were you discussing on the way?
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn "on the way" into a clause.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἐσιώπων, πρὸς ἀλλήλους γὰρ διελέχθησαν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ τίς μείζων.

records.literal_gloss: But they were silent; with one another for they had been discussing on the road who [was] greater.

en.L: But they were silent, for on the road they had been discussing with one another who [was] the greatest.
en.B: They said nothing, because on the way they had been debating among themselves which of them was the greatest.
en.R: But they did not answer. They had been arguing with each other on the road about which one of them was the most important.

es.L: Pero ellos callaban, porque en el camino habían discutido entre sí quién [era el] mayor.
es.B: Ellos no dijeron nada, porque en el camino habían estado discutiendo entre sí cuál de ellos era el más grande.
es.R: Pero ellos no respondieron. En el camino habían estado discutiendo sobre cuál de ellos era el más importante.

sw.L: Lakini wao wakanyamaza, kwa maana njiani walikuwa wamejadiliana wao kwa wao ni nani [aliye] mkuu zaidi.
sw.B: Hawakusema neno, kwa sababu njiani walikuwa wakibishana wao kwa wao ni nani kati yao aliye mkuu kuliko wote.
sw.R: Lakini hawakujibu. Njiani walikuwa wakibishana wao kwa wao ni nani kati yao aliye muhimu kuliko wote.

decisions.choice: greater: the form meaning greater, used here for greatest
decisions.reason: Greek of this time often used the form for "greater" to mean the greatest of a group.

decisions.choice: who: which one of them
decisions.reason: They were comparing themselves with each other.

decisions.choice: they were silent: they kept quiet out of shame
decisions.reason: Their silence follows Jesus' teaching about his death (9:31).

decisions.choice: the most important
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday phrase for greatness in rank.

source.text: καὶ καθίσας ἐφώνησεν τοὺς δώδεκα καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Εἴ τις θέλει πρῶτος εἶναι ἔσται πάντων ἔσχατος καὶ πάντων διάκονος.

records.literal_gloss: And having sat down he called the twelve and says to them, If anyone desires first to be, he will be of all last and of all servant.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat down and called the twelve and says to them, "If anyone wants to be first, {{gender:they|he}} will be last of all and servant of all."
en.B: He sat down, called the Twelve, and said to them, "Whoever wants to be first must be last of everyone and the servant of everyone."
en.R: Jesus sat down and called the Twelve to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He said, "If you want to be the most important, you must put yourself last. You must serve everyone else."

es.L: Y sentándose, llamó a los doce y les dice: «Si alguno quiere ser primero, será el último de todos y servidor de todos».
es.B: Se sentó, llamó a los Doce y les dijo: «Quien quiera ser el primero, tiene que ser el último de todos y el servidor de todos».
es.R: Jesús se sentó y llamó a los Doce a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} lado. Les dijo: «Si quieres ser el más importante, tienes que ponerte en el último lugar. Tienes que servir a todos los demás».

sw.L: Na akaketi, akawaita wale kumi na wawili, na anawaambia, "Mtu yeyote akitaka kuwa wa kwanza, atakuwa wa mwisho wa wote, na mhudumu wa wote."
sw.B: Aliketi, akawaita wale Kumi na Wawili, akawaambia, "Anayetaka kuwa wa kwanza ni lazima awe wa mwisho kuliko wote, na mhudumu wa wote."
sw.R: Yesu aliketi, akawaita wale Kumi na Wawili waje {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}. Akawaambia, "Kama unataka kuwa mtu muhimu kuliko wote, ni lazima ujiweke wa mwisho. Ni lazima uwahudumie wengine wote."

decisions.choice: sat down: the posture of a teacher
decisions.reason: Teachers sat to teach (4:1). The words that follow are formal teaching.

decisions.choice: he will be: a future that works as a command
alternatives: a warning that he will end up last
decisions.reason: The future can state what must be. It could also mean that whoever seeks first place will be put last.

decisions.choice: servant: one who serves others, as at table
decisions.reason: The word is the one for a servant who waits on others. Mark uses the word for slave in 10:44.

decisions.choice: says: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present again.

decisions.choice: If you want to be the most important, you must put yourself last
alternatives: If anyone desires to be first
decisions.reason: Readable speaks to the hearer directly and says what "first" means.

decisions.choice: será, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English Literal needs a pronoun ("they" or "he") and puts it under the gender setting. Spanish leaves the subject in the verb, so there is nothing for the setting to change; the same holds for "le" and "su" in verses 41 and 42.

decisions.choice: Si quieres ... tienes que (R)
decisions.reason: The English Readable "you" stands for "anyone". Spanish says that with the general "tú", which keeps the saying open to every hearer without the plural_you setting.

decisions.choice: mhudumu (L, B); uwahudumie (R)
decisions.reason: The New Testament choice for Swahili: "mhudumu" is one who serves others, as at table (meaning decision m3), and keeps "mtumishi" for the Greek word for slave. Swahili needs no gender span where the English Literal has "they|he": the subject is in the verb.

source.text: καὶ λαβὼν παιδίον ἔστησεν αὐτὸ ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῶν καὶ ἐναγκαλισάμενος αὐτὸ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς·

records.literal_gloss: And having taken a child he set it in [the] midst of them, and having taken in arms it he said to them,

en.L: And taking a child, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} set it in the middle of them, and taking it in [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] arms, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them,
en.B: He took a little child and stood the child among them. Then, putting {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} arms around the child, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them,
en.R: Then Jesus took a little child and had the child stand in front of them. He took the child in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} arms and said to them,

es.L: Y tomando a un niño, lo puso en medio de ellos, y abrazándolo, les dijo:
es.B: Tomó a un niño pequeño y lo puso en medio de ellos. Luego, rodeándolo con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} brazos, les dijo:
es.R: Entonces Jesús tomó a un niño pequeño y lo puso de pie delante de ellos. Tomó al niño en {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} brazos y les dijo:

sw.L: Na akimchukua mtoto mdogo, akamsimamisha katikati yao, na akimkumbatia, akawaambia,
sw.B: Alimchukua mtoto mdogo, akamsimamisha katikati yao. Kisha akamkumbatia, akawaambia,
sw.R: Kisha Yesu alimchukua mtoto mdogo, akamsimamisha mbele yao. Akamkumbatia mikononi {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}, akawaambia,

decisions.choice: a child: someone with no rank or importance
decisions.reason: Children had no standing in that society. Jesus answers the debate about greatness by setting one in the middle.

decisions.choice: taking in his arms: embracing
decisions.reason: The verb means to hold in the arms. Mark uses it again in 10:16.

decisions.choice: it: the word for child is neuter
decisions.reason: Mark does not say whether the child was a boy or a girl.

decisions.choice: the child
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable avoid calling a child "it".

decisions.choice: abrazándolo
decisions.reason: The Greek is one verb, "embracing" (meaning decision m2). Spanish has the same single verb, so Literal needs no supplied words where the English Literal supplies "his".

source.text: Ὃς ἂν ἓν τῶν τοιούτων παιδίων δέξηται ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου, ἐμὲ δέχεται· καὶ ὃς ἂν ἐμὲ δέχηται, οὐκ ἐμὲ δέχεται ἀλλὰ τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με.

records.literal_gloss: Whoever one of such little children shall receive in the name of me, me receives; and whoever me shall receive, not me receives but the [One] having sent me.

en.L: "Whoever receives one of such children in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name receives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; and whoever receives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} receives not {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} but the One who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.B: "Whoever welcomes a child like this one in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name is welcoming {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. And whoever welcomes {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is welcoming, not {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, but the One who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.R: "When someone welcomes a little child like this for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sake, they are welcoming {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. And when they welcome {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, they are not only welcoming {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They are also welcoming God, who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

es.L: «Quien acoja a uno de tales niños en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre, a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} acoge; y quien a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} acoja, no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} acoge a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, sino al que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió».
es.B: «Quien acoge a un niño como este en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} está acogiendo a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Y quien {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} acoge no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} acoge a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, sino al que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió».
es.R: «Cuando alguien recibe a un niño pequeño como este por amor a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} está recibiendo a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Y cuando {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} recibe a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, no solo {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} está recibiendo a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. También está recibiendo a Dios, que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió».

sw.L: "Yeyote atakayemkaribisha mmoja wa watoto wadogo kama hawa kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, ananikaribisha {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}; na yeyote atakayenikaribisha {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, hanikaribishi {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, bali {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} aliyenituma.
sw.B: "Mtu yeyote anayemkaribisha mtoto kama huyu kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, ananikaribisha {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}. Na mtu anayenikaribisha {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, hanikaribishi {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, bali anamkaribisha {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} aliyenituma.
sw.R: "Mtu anapomkaribisha mtoto mdogo kama huyu kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, ananikaribisha {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}. Na anaponikaribisha {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, hanikaribishi {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} peke yangu. Anamkaribisha pia Mungu, aliyenituma.

decisions.choice: in my name: for my sake, because the child belongs to me
alternatives: using my name as a formula
decisions.reason: To do something in someone's name is to do it on their account.

decisions.choice: not me but the one who sent me: not only me but also God
alternatives: they do not receive Jesus at all
decisions.reason: "Not this but that" is a common way of putting stress on the second item. Receiving Jesus is receiving God.

decisions.choice: receive: welcome as a guest
decisions.reason: The verb is used for showing hospitality (6:11).

decisions.choice: the One who sent me: God
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of himself as sent by the Father, as in 12:6.

decisions.choice: for my sake; not only ... also; God
alternatives: in my name; not me but the One who sent me
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idioms and names God as the sender.

decisions.choice: acoger (L, B); recibir (R)
decisions.reason: Receiving here is welcoming someone as a guest (meaning decision m3); "acoger" says that, as in Matthew 10:40. Readable says "recibir", the everyday word for having a guest.

decisions.choice: kukaribisha
decisions.reason: Receiving here is welcoming someone as a guest (meaning decision m3); "kukaribisha" says that, as in Matthew 10:40, where "kupokea" can mean simply taking something handed over.

source.text: Ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰωάννης· Διδάσκαλε, εἴδομέν τινα ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου ἐκβάλλοντα δαιμόνια, καὶ ἐκωλύομεν αὐτόν, ὅτι οὐκ ἠκολούθει ἡμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: Said to him John, Teacher, we saw someone in the name of you casting out demons, and we were forbidding him, because not he was following us.

en.L: John said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, and we tried to stop him, because he was not following us."
en.B: John said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, we saw a man throwing out demons in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name. We tried to stop him, since he did not go around with us."
en.R: John said to Jesus, "Teacher, we saw a man using {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name to force demons to leave people. We told him to stop, because he was not one of our group."

es.L: Juan {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Maestro, vimos a uno que expulsaba demonios en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre, y tratábamos de impedírselo, porque no nos seguía».
es.B: Juan {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Maestro, vimos a un hombre que expulsaba demonios en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre. Intentamos impedírselo, porque no andaba con nosotros».
es.R: Juan dijo a Jesús: «Maestro, vimos a un hombre que usaba {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre para obligar a los demonios a salir de la gente. Le dijimos que no lo hiciera, porque no era de nuestro grupo».

sw.L: Yohana akamwambia, "Mwalimu, tulimwona mtu akitoa pepo kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}, nasi tukajaribu kumzuia, kwa sababu hakuwa akitufuata."
sw.B: Yohana alimwambia, "Mwalimu, tulimwona mtu mmoja akifukuza pepo kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}. Tulijaribu kumzuia, kwa sababu hakuwa akiandamana nasi."
sw.R: Yohana alimwambia Yesu, "Mwalimu, tulimwona mtu akilitumia jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}} kuwalazimisha pepo kuwatoka watu. Tukamwambia aache, kwa sababu yeye si mmoja wa kikundi chetu."

decisions.choice: we were forbidding: we tried to stop him
decisions.reason: The imperfect can describe an attempt. It is not clear whether the man obeyed.

decisions.choice: in your name: calling on Jesus' name to drive out demons
decisions.reason: Exorcists used the names of powerful figures. Acts 19:13 tells of men who tried using the name of Jesus.

decisions.choice: following us: not one of the disciples' company
decisions.reason: John says "us", not "you". The concern is about belonging to their group.

decisions.choice: the wording of the SBLGNT
alternatives: add: who does not follow us
decisions.reason: Later manuscripts add "who does not follow us" after "demons" and vary the order of the clauses. The meaning is not changed. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: throwing out (B); force to leave people (R)
decisions.reason: The pattern of earlier chapters.

decisions.choice: demonios
decisions.reason: The New Testament choice for Spanish: "demonio" at every level for this word, as in Mark 16:9 and Matthew 17:18.

decisions.choice: pepo
decisions.reason: The New Testament choice for Swahili: "pepo" at every level for this word, as in Matthew 17:18. "Shetani" is kept for Satan himself.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Μὴ κωλύετε αὐτόν, οὐδεὶς γάρ ἐστιν ὃς ποιήσει δύναμιν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου καὶ δυνήσεται ταχὺ κακολογῆσαί με·

records.literal_gloss: But Jesus said, Not forbid him, no one for there is who will do a work of power in the name of me and will be able readily to speak evil of me;

en.L: But Jesus said, "Do not stop him, for there is no one who will do a work of power in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name and be able soon afterward to speak evil of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}};
en.B: Jesus said, "Do not stop him. No one who does a mighty work in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name will be quick to speak ill of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} afterward.
en.R: But Jesus said, "Do not stop him. A person who does a powerful miracle by using {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name will not soon turn around and say bad things about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Pero Jesús dijo: «No se lo {{plural_you:impidan|impidáis}}, porque no hay nadie que haga una obra poderosa en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre y que pueda luego hablar mal de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}};
es.B: Jesús dijo: «No se lo {{plural_you:impidan|impidáis}}. Nadie que haga una obra poderosa en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre se apresurará después a hablar mal de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.R: Pero Jesús dijo: «No se lo {{plural_you:impidan|impidáis}}. Una persona que hace un milagro usando {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre no va a ponerse luego a hablar mal de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.

sw.L: Lakini Yesu akasema, "Msimzuie, kwa maana hakuna mtu atakayefanya tendo la nguvu kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, kisha akaweza upesi kunisema vibaya;
sw.B: Yesu alisema, "Msimzuie. Hakuna mtu atendaye tendo la nguvu kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} atakayekuwa mwepesi kunisema vibaya baadaye.
sw.R: Lakini Yesu akasema, "Msimzuie. Mtu anayefanya muujiza kwa kutumia jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} hatageuka upesi na kunisema vibaya.

decisions.choice: do not stop him: a present command, stop trying to prevent him
decisions.reason: The form tells them to give up what they were doing.

decisions.choice: soon afterward: quickly, readily
decisions.reason: The adverb means quickly. A man who has just done a mighty deed in Jesus' name will not turn at once to speak against him.

decisions.choice: work of power: a miracle
decisions.reason: The same word as in 6:2 and 6:5.

decisions.choice: will not soon turn around and say bad things about me
alternatives: will be able readily to speak evil of me
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for the idiom.

decisions.choice: una obra poderosa (L, B); un milagro (R)
decisions.reason: The New Testament choice for Spanish: "obras poderosas" keeps the Greek word for power (meaning decision m3); Readable says "milagro", as the English Readable says "miracle".

decisions.choice: tendo la nguvu (L, B); muujiza (R)
decisions.reason: The New Testament choice for Swahili: "matendo ya nguvu" keeps the Greek word for power (meaning decision m3); Readable says "muujiza", as the English Readable says "miracle".

source.text: ὃς γὰρ οὐκ ἔστιν καθ’ ἡμῶν, ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: whoever for not is against us, for us is.

en.L: for whoever is not against us is for us.
en.B: Anyone not against us is for us.
en.R: If people are not against us, they are on our side.

es.L: pues el que no está contra nosotros, por nosotros está.
es.B: Quien no está contra nosotros está a nuestro favor.
es.R: Si alguien no está en contra de nosotros, está de nuestro lado.

sw.L: kwa maana yeye asiyekuwa kinyume chetu yuko upande wetu.
sw.B: Mtu ambaye hayuko kinyume chetu yuko upande wetu.
sw.R: Kama watu hawako kinyume chetu, basi wako upande wetu.

decisions.choice: us, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "against you ... for you". The SBLGNT reads "us", which includes Jesus with his disciples. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: not against us is for us: a generous rule for those who act in Jesus' name
decisions.reason: Matthew 12:30 gives the reverse: whoever is not with me is against me. There Jesus speaks of those who oppose him; here of one who acts in his name.

decisions.choice: on our side
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday phrase.

source.text: Ὃς γὰρ ἂν ποτίσῃ ὑμᾶς ποτήριον ὕδατος ἐν ὀνόματι ὅτι χριστοῦ ἐστε, ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐ μὴ ἀπολέσῃ τὸν μισθὸν αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Whoever for might give to drink you a cup of water in name that of Christ you are, truly I say to you that no not shall he lose the reward of him.

en.L: For whoever gives you a cup of water to drink in [the] name that you belong to the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, truly I say to you that {{gender:they|he}} will by no means lose {{gender:their|his}} reward.
en.B: If anyone gives you a cup of water to drink because you belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, truly I tell you, that person will certainly not lose the reward.
en.R: I tell you the truth: if someone gives you so much as a cup of water because you belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, God will surely reward that person.

es.L: Porque cualquiera que {{plural_you:les|os}} dé a beber un vaso de agua en nombre de que {{plural_you:son|sois}} {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}, en verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que de ningún modo perderá su recompensa.
es.B: Si alguien {{plural_you:les|os}} da a beber un vaso de agua porque {{plural_you:pertenecen|pertenecéis}} {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}, en verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que esa persona de ningún modo perderá su recompensa.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: si alguien {{plural_you:les|os}} da aunque sea un vaso de agua porque {{plural_you:pertenecen|pertenecéis}} {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}, Dios le dará con toda seguridad su recompensa.

sw.L: Kwa maana yeyote atakayewanywesha kikombe cha maji kwa jina la kwamba ninyi ni wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, kweli nawaambia, hatapoteza kamwe ujira wake.
sw.B: Mtu yeyote atakayewapa kikombe cha maji mnywe kwa sababu ninyi ni wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, kweli nawaambia, mtu huyo hatakosa kamwe ujira wake.
sw.R: Nawaambia ukweli, mtu akiwapa hata kikombe cha maji tu kwa sababu ninyi ni wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, Mungu hakika atampa mtu huyo ujira wake.

decisions.choice: in name that you are Christ's: because you belong to Christ
decisions.reason: The phrase means on the ground that, or because. The gift is given to the disciples as Christ's people.

decisions.choice: Christ: the Messiah, God's anointed king
decisions.reason: Jesus rarely uses the title of himself in Mark. Peter has just confessed him as the Christ (8:29).

decisions.choice: in name that you are Christ's, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: in my name, because you are Christ's
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "in my name". Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: his reward: the giver's reward from God
decisions.reason: Even the smallest kindness to Christ's people is seen and rewarded by God.

decisions.choice: so much as; God will surely reward
alternatives: will by no means lose the reward
decisions.reason: Readable says the promise positively and names God as the one who rewards. "So much as" brings out how small the gift is.

decisions.choice: {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}} (L); {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Spanish takes the preposition into the span where the article contracts ("del", "al"), so both forms read correctly (meaning decision m2).

source.text: Καὶ ὃς ἂν σκανδαλίσῃ ἕνα τῶν μικρῶν τούτων τῶν πιστευόντων εἰς ἐμέ, καλόν ἐστιν αὐτῷ μᾶλλον εἰ περίκειται μύλος ὀνικὸς περὶ τὸν τράχηλον αὐτοῦ καὶ βέβληται εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν.

records.literal_gloss: And whoever might cause to stumble one of the little ones these, the believing in me, better it is for him rather if is put a millstone of a donkey around the neck of him and he has been cast into the sea.

en.L: And whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to stumble, it is better for {{gender:them|him}} if a donkey's millstone is put around {{gender:their|his}} neck and {{gender:they are|he is}} thrown into the sea.
en.B: Whoever makes one of these little ones who believe in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} fall away would be better off having a huge millstone hung around the neck and being thrown into the sea.
en.R: Suppose someone leads one of these little ones who believe in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} into sin. It would be better for that person to have a heavy stone for grinding grain tied around the neck and be thrown into the sea.

es.L: Y cualquiera que haga tropezar a uno de estos pequeños que creen en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, mejor le es si se le pone alrededor del cuello una piedra de molino de asno y es arrojado al mar.
es.B: Al que haga caer a uno de estos pequeños que creen en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, más le valdría que le colgaran al cuello una enorme piedra de molino y lo arrojaran al mar.
es.R: Supongamos que alguien hace pecar a uno de estos pequeños que creen en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Sería mejor para esa persona que le ataran al cuello una piedra pesada de las que se usan para moler grano, y que la tiraran al mar.

sw.L: Na yeyote atakayemkwaza mmoja wa wadogo hawa wanaoniamini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, ni afadhali kwake kama jiwe la kusagia linalozungushwa na punda likifungwa shingoni mwake, na kutupwa baharini.
sw.B: Mtu yeyote atakayemfanya mmoja wa wadogo hawa wanaoniamini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} aanguke kutoka kwenye imani, ingekuwa afadhali kwake afungiwe shingoni jiwe kubwa la kusagia na kutupwa baharini.
sw.R: Tuseme mtu fulani anamfanya mmoja wa wadogo hawa wanaoniamini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} atende dhambi. Ingekuwa afadhali kwa mtu huyo afungwe shingoni jiwe zito la kusagia nafaka, na kutupwa baharini.

decisions.choice: cause to stumble: cause to fall into sin or away from faith
decisions.reason: The verb means to trip someone up. In Mark it is used of falling away (4:17; 14:27).

decisions.choice: a donkey's millstone: the large upper stone of a mill turned by a donkey
decisions.reason: The word describes a millstone so heavy that an animal was needed to turn it. A man with one around his neck would sink at once.

decisions.choice: these little ones who believe in me: humble believers, like the child of 9:36
decisions.reason: "Little ones" follows the child Jesus held, but "who believe in me" shows that his followers are meant, however small.

decisions.choice: in me, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts lack "in me". The SBLGNT includes it. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: fall away (B); sin (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the stumbling is.

decisions.choice: a heavy stone for grinding grain
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a millstone is.

decisions.choice: piedra de molino de asno (L); una enorme piedra de molino (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek names the large upper stone of a mill turned by a donkey (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps the donkey; Balanced says what it means for the hearer, its size, as the English "huge millstone" does.

decisions.choice: jiwe la kusagia linalozungushwa na punda (L); jiwe kubwa la kusagia (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek names the large upper stone of a mill turned by a donkey (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps the donkey; Balanced says what it means for the hearer, its size, as the English "huge millstone" does.

source.text: Καὶ ἐὰν σκανδαλίζῃ σε ἡ χείρ σου, ἀπόκοψον αὐτήν· καλόν ἐστίν σε κυλλὸν εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν ζωὴν ἢ τὰς δύο χεῖρας ἔχοντα ἀπελθεῖν εἰς τὴν γέενναν, εἰς τὸ πῦρ τὸ ἄσβεστον.

records.literal_gloss: And if causes to stumble you the hand of you, cut off it; better it is for you maimed to enter into the life than the two hands having to go away into the Gehenna, into the fire the unquenchable.

en.L: And if your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off; it is better for you to enter into life maimed than having two hands to go away into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire.
en.B: If your hand leads you into sin, cut it off. You are better off entering life maimed than going off with both hands into hell, into the fire that cannot be put out.
en.R: If your hand makes you sin, cut it off. It is better to have only one hand and enter into life with God than to keep both hands and go to hell. Hell is the place where the fire never goes out.

es.L: Y si tu mano te hace tropezar, córtala; mejor te es entrar manco en la vida que, teniendo las dos manos, ir a la Gehena, al fuego inextinguible.
es.B: Si tu mano te lleva a pecar, córtatela. Más te vale entrar manco en la vida que ir con las dos manos al infierno, al fuego que no se puede apagar.
es.R: Si tu mano te hace pecar, córtatela. Es mejor tener una sola mano y entrar en la vida con Dios que conservar las dos manos e ir al infierno. El infierno es el lugar donde el fuego nunca se apaga.

sw.L: Na kama mkono wako unakukwaza, ukate; ni afadhali kwako kuingia katika uzima ukiwa kilema kuliko kuwa na mikono miwili na kwenda Gehena, katika moto usiozimika.
sw.B: Mkono wako ukikuongoza dhambini, ukate. Ni afadhali kwako kuingia katika uzima ukiwa umekatika mkono, kuliko kwenda jehanamu na mikono yako miwili, katika moto usioweza kuzimwa.
sw.R: Mkono wako ukikufanya utende dhambi, ukate. Ni afadhali kuwa na mkono mmoja tu na kuingia katika uzima pamoja na Mungu, kuliko kubaki na mikono yote miwili na kwenda jehanamu. Jehanamu ni mahali ambapo moto hauzimiki kamwe.

decisions.choice: Gehenna: the Valley of Hinnom, a name for the place of final judgment
decisions.reason: The Valley of Hinnom lay south of Jerusalem. Children had been burned there as sacrifices to idols (2 Kings 23:10; Jeremiah 7:31), and its name came to stand for the fire of God's judgment, as in Matthew 5:22.

decisions.choice: the unquenchable fire: fire that no one can put out
alternatives: a fire that burns for a while
decisions.reason: The fire of judgment cannot be stopped (Isaiah 66:24; Matthew 3:12).

decisions.choice: life: the life of the age to come
decisions.reason: "Life" here stands in parallel with "the kingdom of God" in 9:47.

decisions.choice: cut it off: get rid of whatever leads to sin, at any cost
decisions.reason: The picture is deliberately extreme. Losing a hand is better than losing everything.

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT has no verse 44
alternatives: add verse 44: where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add here the words of 9:48, which also follow 9:45 in those manuscripts (verse 46). The earliest manuscripts lack them, and scribes likely copied the line from 9:48 to make the three sayings match. Verse 44 is skipped in the numbering for this reason. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: Gehenna (L); hell (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the place name, as in Matthew 5:22. Balanced and Readable use the English word for the place of final judgment.

decisions.choice: life with God; Hell is the place where the fire never goes out
decisions.reason: Readable explains what life and hell mean here in short sentences.

decisions.choice: la Gehena (L); el infierno (B, R)
decisions.reason: The New Testament choice: Literal keeps the place name (meaning decision m1), and Balanced and Readable say "infierno", as the English says "hell" and as in Matthew 5:29-30. The same in verses 45 and 47.

decisions.choice: Gehena (L); jehanamu (B, R)

source.text: καὶ ἐὰν ὁ πούς σου σκανδαλίζῃ σε, ἀπόκοψον αὐτόν· καλόν ἐστίν σε εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν ζωὴν χωλὸν ἢ τοὺς δύο πόδας ἔχοντα βληθῆναι εἰς τὴν γέενναν.

records.literal_gloss: And if the foot of you causes to stumble you, cut off it; better it is for you to enter into the life lame than the two feet having to be cast into the Gehenna.

en.L: And if your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off; it is better for you to enter into life lame than having two feet to be thrown into Gehenna.
en.B: If your foot leads you into sin, cut it off. You are better off entering life lame than being thrown into hell with both feet.
en.R: If your foot makes you sin, cut it off. It is better to be lame and enter into life with God than to keep both feet and be thrown into hell.

es.L: Y si tu pie te hace tropezar, córtalo; mejor te es entrar cojo en la vida que, teniendo los dos pies, ser arrojado a la Gehena.
es.B: Si tu pie te lleva a pecar, córtatelo. Más te vale entrar cojo en la vida que ser arrojado al infierno con los dos pies.
es.R: Si tu pie te hace pecar, córtatelo. Es mejor ser cojo y entrar en la vida con Dios que conservar los dos pies y ser arrojado al infierno.

sw.L: Na kama mguu wako unakukwaza, ukate; ni afadhali kwako kuingia katika uzima ukiwa kiwete kuliko kuwa na miguu miwili na kutupwa katika Gehena.
sw.B: Mguu wako ukikuongoza dhambini, ukate. Ni afadhali kwako kuingia katika uzima ukiwa kiwete, kuliko kutupwa jehanamu ukiwa na miguu yote miwili.
sw.R: Mguu wako ukikufanya utende dhambi, ukate. Ni afadhali kuwa kiwete na kuingia katika uzima pamoja na Mungu, kuliko kubaki na miguu yote miwili na kutupwa jehanamu.

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT has no verse 46
alternatives: add verse 46: where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched
decisions.reason: As with verse 44, many later manuscripts repeat here the words of 9:48. The earliest manuscripts lack them, and they are likely a copy of 9:48. Verse 46 is skipped in the numbering for this reason. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: into Gehenna, the end of the saying in the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some later manuscripts add "into the unquenchable fire", as in 9:43. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: to be thrown: a passive, the judgment of God
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the actor unnamed. The one who judges is God.

decisions.choice: hell
decisions.reason: As in 9:43.

source.text: καὶ ἐὰν ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου σκανδαλίζῃ σε, ἔκβαλε αὐτόν· καλόν σέ ἐστιν μονόφθαλμον εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ ἢ δύο ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχοντα βληθῆναι εἰς τὴν γέενναν, ὅπου ὁ σκώληξ αὐτῶν οὐ τελευτᾷ καὶ τὸ πῦρ οὐ σβέννυται.

records.literal_gloss: And if the eye of you causes to stumble you, cast out it; better for you it is one-eyed to enter into the kingdom of God than two eyes having to be cast into the Gehenna, \v 48 where the worm of them not dies and the fire not is quenched.

en.L: And if your eye causes you to stumble, throw it out; it is better for you to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye than having two eyes to be thrown into Gehenna, \v 48 where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.
en.B: If your eye leads you into sin, tear it out. You are better off entering the kingdom of God with only one eye than being thrown into hell with two, \v 48 where the worm that eats them never dies and the fire is never put out.
en.R: If your eye makes you sin, take it out. It is better to have only one eye and enter the kingdom of God than to keep both eyes and be thrown into hell. \v 48 In that place the worms that eat people never die, and the fire never goes out.

es.L: Y si tu ojo te hace tropezar, échalo fuera; mejor te es entrar tuerto en el reino de Dios que, teniendo dos ojos, ser arrojado a la Gehena, \v 48 donde su gusano no muere y el fuego no se apaga.
es.B: Si tu ojo te lleva a pecar, arráncatelo. Más te vale entrar con un solo ojo en el reino de Dios que ser arrojado al infierno con los dos, \v 48 donde el gusano que los devora no muere nunca y el fuego nunca se apaga.
es.R: Si tu ojo te hace pecar, sácatelo. Es mejor tener un solo ojo y entrar en el reino de Dios que conservar los dos ojos y ser arrojado al infierno. \v 48 En ese lugar, los gusanos que se comen a la gente nunca mueren, y el fuego nunca se apaga.

sw.L: Na kama jicho lako linakukwaza, litoe; ni afadhali kwako kuingia katika ufalme wa Mungu ukiwa na jicho moja, kuliko kuwa na macho mawili na kutupwa katika Gehena, \v 48 ambako funza wao hafi, na moto hauzimiki.
sw.B: Jicho lako likikuongoza dhambini, ling'oe. Ni afadhali kwako kuingia katika ufalme wa Mungu ukiwa na jicho moja, kuliko kutupwa jehanamu ukiwa na macho mawili, \v 48 mahali ambapo funza anayewala hafi kamwe, na moto hauzimwi kamwe.
sw.R: Jicho lako likikufanya utende dhambi, liondoe. Ni afadhali kuwa na jicho moja tu na kuingia katika ufalme wa Mungu, kuliko kubaki na macho yote mawili na kutupwa jehanamu. \v 48 Huko funza wanaowala watu hawafi kamwe, na moto hauzimiki kamwe.

decisions.choice: their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched: the last verse of Isaiah
decisions.reason: Isaiah 66:24 describes the dead bodies of those who rebelled against God, eaten by worms and burned by fire that never ends.

decisions.choice: throw it out: the same verb as casting out demons
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the strong verb for driving out: get rid of it.

decisions.choice: the kingdom of God: the same as life in 9:43 and 9:45
decisions.reason: The three sayings set "life" and "the kingdom of God" side by side as the same goal.

decisions.choice: their worm: the worm that feeds on those thrown there
alternatives: the worm that belongs to them as a pet
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers to the people in Gehenna.

decisions.choice: tear it out (B); take it out (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a verb that fits an eye. Literal keeps "throw out".

decisions.choice: hell
decisions.reason: As in 9:43.

decisions.choice: litoe (L); ling'oe (B); liondoe (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is the one used for casting out demons (meaning decision m2). Literal says "litoe", the verb of "kutoa pepo" in verses 18 and 38, so the link shows; Balanced says "ling'oe" (tear it out), as the English does.

records.literal_gloss: Everyone for with fire will be salted.

en.L: For everyone will be salted with fire.
en.B: Everyone will be salted with fire.
en.R: Every person will be salted with fire.

es.L: Porque todos serán salados con fuego.
es.B: Todos serán salados con fuego.
es.R: Cada persona será salada con fuego.

sw.L: Kwa maana kila mtu atatiwa chumvi kwa moto.
sw.B: Kila mtu atatiwa chumvi kwa moto.
sw.R: Kila mmoja atatiwa chumvi kwa moto.

decisions.choice: everyone will be salted with fire, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: add: and every sacrifice will be salted with salt
every sacrifice will be salted with salt (in place of the saying)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "and every sacrifice will be salted with salt", and some have that line instead. It comes from Leviticus 2:13, where every grain offering was to be seasoned with salt, and was likely added by scribes to explain the saying. The earliest manuscripts have only the shorter text. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: salted with fire: everyone will be tested and purified, as a sacrifice is salted
alternatives: the wicked will be kept in the fire of judgment
disciples will be refined by suffering
decisions.reason: The saying is one of the hardest in Mark. "For" links it to the fire of 9:48. It may mean that every disciple will be made pure through trial, as offerings were salted (Leviticus 2:13). It may also mean that those in judgment are preserved in the fire. Mark does not explain it.

decisions.choice: for: the saying explains what came before
decisions.reason: The word ties the salt to the fire of the previous saying.

decisions.choice: Every person will be salted with fire
alternatives: everyone will be purified by fire
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture rather than choose one explanation, because the meaning is uncertain.

source.text: καλὸν τὸ ἅλας· ἐὰν δὲ τὸ ἅλας ἄναλον γένηται, ἐν τίνι αὐτὸ ἀρτύσετε;

records.literal_gloss: Good [is] the salt; if however the salt unsalty becomes, with what it will you season?

en.L: Salt [is] good; but if the salt becomes unsalty, with what will you season it?
en.B: Salt is a good thing. But if the salt stops being salty, how will you give it back its flavor?
en.R: Salt is good. But if salt loses its taste, nothing can make it salty again.

es.L: Buena [es] la sal; pero si la sal se vuelve insípida, ¿con qué la {{plural_you:sazonarán|sazonaréis}}?
es.B: La sal es buena. Pero si la sal deja de ser salada, ¿cómo le {{plural_you:devolverán|devolveréis}} su sabor?
es.R: La sal es buena. Pero si la sal pierde su sabor, nada puede volver a hacerla salada.

sw.L: Chumvi [ni] njema; lakini chumvi ikikosa uchumvi, mtaikoleza kwa kitu gani?
sw.B: Chumvi ni kitu kizuri. Lakini chumvi ikiacha kuwa na chumvi, mtairudishiaje ladha yake?
sw.R: Chumvi ni nzuri. Lakini chumvi ikipoteza ladha yake, hakuna kitu kinachoweza kuifanya iwe na chumvi tena.

decisions.choice: salt becomes unsalty: impure salt could lose its taste
decisions.reason: Salt gathered from the Dead Sea was mixed with other minerals. When the salt was washed out by damp, what was left looked like salt but had no taste.

decisions.choice: with what will you season it: a question expecting the answer, nothing
alternatives: a real request for a method
decisions.reason: Salt that has lost its taste cannot be restored.

decisions.choice: season: give it flavor
decisions.reason: The verb means to season food.

decisions.choice: nothing can make it salty again
alternatives: with what will you season it?
decisions.reason: Readable gives the answer the question expects.

decisions.choice: in yourselves: within each of you, or among you as a group
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean in each person or among the company. With "one another" following, both may be in view.

decisions.choice: salt: the mark of a true disciple, perhaps also of a covenant shared
decisions.reason: Salt was part of God's covenant with Israel (Leviticus 2:13; Numbers 18:19), and sharing salt meant friendship. The call to be at peace answers the quarrel about greatness (9:34).

decisions.choice: be at peace: live in peace, the verb form of peace
decisions.reason: The verb is about relations between people.

decisions.choice: in your lives
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain phrase that keeps the open sense.
